AAI 520 Final — Investment Research Agent (Colab)¶

GitHub repository: https://github.com/dshrestha37/investment-research-agent

One ticker in, one cited analyst note out. This notebook is the integration of:

  • Deepika Shrestha, Investment_Research_Agent_Deepika_Shrestha_09_29_2026_Github_Upload.ipynb — plan, tools, chain, router, evaluator, memory.
  • Christian Lopez, News_Ingestion_Pipeline.ipynb — Yahoo headlines, category tag, FAISS side index.
  • Cameron Aljilani — integration of both notebooks, bug fixes (router phrase, Claude model id, empty-news fail-closed, synthetic-article removal, "No news retrieved" summary bug, Gemini-mode evaluator/citation/truncation/lesson fixes), news relevance filters, evidence and visualization cells, Colab wrapper, and executed runs.

Ticker is set in the next cell and nowhere else. No company name, sector, or peer is hardcoded. This run uses TICKER = "AAPL", but it can be changed to any Yahoo symbol (for example DIS or META).

Each %%writefile cell is a fixed module. The change log is the module docstring.

File What changed from their original
router.py pos = "between" printed "trading between of its averages". Phrases are now complete. The News specialist no longer says "No news retrieved" when every article was routed to the Earnings specialist.

Gemini (the path this notebook uses) now reads its model from GEMINI_MODEL (default gemini-3.8-flash), allows 8192 output tokens, flags truncated replies (MAX_TOKENS), and reports calls/errors through llm_status.

evaluator.py Section check tolerates the heading variants Gemini writes (it had scored complete notes as "Missing sections: all 8"); combined citations [S2, S3] count; truncated drafts are flagged; the writer prompt names the exact headings; the writer now sees the prior run and the "Changes since last run" lines.

schema.py, market_tools.py, extra_tools.py Reviewed. No behavior change.

Run top to bottom. Step "Tests" needs no keys. Step "Run" needs a Gemini key for LLM mode; without it the rule-based path still produces a note. The LLM status line under each run states which path this run actually used.

AI disclosure:

  • Google Gemini (gemini-3.8-flash via the google-genai API) is an optional runtime component of the agent. When GEMINI_API_KEY is set, the agent asks it to plan, classify/extract/summarize news, draft, judge, and refine the note. Every LLM step is gated and has a rule-based fallback.
  • Cameron Aljilani used Grok (xAI) for integration, debugging, and documentation guidance: Colab setup, the news-relevance filters (financial NewsAPI query, post-filter, preprocess gate), diagnosing and fixing the "No news retrieved" summary bug and the failing offline test, the evidence and visualization cells, and Gemini-mode fixes (evaluator section check, combined citations, truncation handling, lesson de-duplication, prior-run context for the writer).
  • Christian Lopez: Used Gemini (Google) for coding assistance on the news ingestion pipeline (News_Ingestion_Pipeline.ipynb), including the Yahoo Finance fetch, the classifier, and the FAISS index.

All AI-suggested code was read, tested (offline tests in section 4 and the two executed runs), and modified where needed by the team, and we can explain every module. No citation, metric, or news article in the note is produced without a fetched source.

1 — Install¶

Do not upgrade Torch. The news notebook's pip install --upgrade torch was unnecessary for MiniLM and slowed the runtime.

These packages supply the tool layer (yfinance), the optional LLM path (google-genai), and the FAISS side index. No model is trained; everything is inference or API calls.

2 — Secrets¶

Put keys in Colab Secrets (key icon, left sidebar), not in this cell. Names:

  • GEMINI_API_KEY — LLM mode. Without it the agent uses rule fallbacks and still writes a note.
  • NEWSAPI_KEY — optional. Without it, news comes from Yahoo.
  • FRED_API_KEY — optional macro series.
  • SEC_USER_AGENT — a contact string, not a password. EDGAR requires it. Example: AAI520-IRA you@school.edu.

This cell only copies secrets into the process environment. Keys stay out of the notebook so the same file can be shared and graded without exposing credentials. The agent still produces a complete note via rule fallbacks when GEMINI_API_KEY is absent.

In [3]:
import os  # process environment the modules already read


# Keys stay in Colab Secrets, never in the notebook, so the shared and
# graded file exposes no credentials.
def load_secret(name):  # copy one Colab secret into os.environ; no-op outside Colab
    try:
        from google.colab import userdata  # only exists on Colab
        value = userdata.get(name)  # raises if the secret is missing, caught below
    except Exception:
        value = None  # local Jupyter, or secret not set
    if value:
        os.environ[name] = value.strip()  # modules call os.getenv
    return bool(os.environ.get(name))  # True if a key is available for this name


needed = ["GEMINI_API_KEY", "NEWSAPI_KEY", "FRED_API_KEY", "SEC_USER_AGENT"]  # the four the tools look up
print({k: load_secret(k) for k in needed})  # True/False only; values are not printed

# SEC EDGAR needs no API key, only a contact User-Agent (SEC fair-access policy). SEC_USER_AGENT was not set
# for this run, so extra_tools used its generic default; set it in Colab Secrets to "Name your@sandiego.edu".

{'GEMINI_API_KEY': True, 'NEWSAPI_KEY': True, 'FRED_API_KEY': True, 'SEC_USER_AGENT': False}

3 — Write the fixed modules¶

Agent Design and Workflows¶

TICKER (one cell)
  │
  ▼
PLAN ─ research_agent.plan(): LLM or rule plan, mandatory-tool safeguard, reads lessons from memory
  │
  ▼
ACT ─ tools, each returns a ToolResult cited as [S#]
      recall_memory · get_price_history · get_fundamentals · fetch_news · get_macro · get_edgar_filings
      (one retry on transient errors; fewer than 5 articles → widened news query)
  │
  ▼
WORKFLOW 1 ─ PROMPT CHAIN (chain.py): ingest → preprocess → classify → extract → summarize → articles [N#]
  │
  ▼
WORKFLOW 2 ─ ROUTING (router.py): Market · Earnings & Fundamentals · News specialists
  │
  ▼
WORKFLOW 3 ─ EVALUATOR–OPTIMIZER (evaluator.py): draft → score 5 criteria → refine (up to 3 rounds)
  │
  ▼
REFLECT & LEARN ─ research_agent.reflect() + memory.py: metrics + lessons → ira_state/memory.json → next run

Each module below implements one piece of this design. Every tool returns a ToolResult and never raises. The chain, router, and evaluator are the three workflow patterns. Memory is the only state that persists across runs. The modules are written with %%writefile, and each docstring is the change log for the teammate who wrote the original.

schema.py¶

In [4]:
%%writefile schema.py
"""Shared ToolResult schema: every tool in the agent returns this shape.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (schema.py):
- No behavioral change. Header note added so the teammate can see the file was reviewed.
- ToolResult is the single contract every tool must obey. ok=False plus an error string
- lets the agent continue and disclose the gap instead of crashing.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


@dataclass
class ToolResult:
    tool: str
    ok: bool
    data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    error: str | None = None
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    source: str = ""
    fetched_at: str = field(default_factory=_now)

    @classmethod
    def success(cls, tool, data, source="", warnings=None) -> "ToolResult":
        return cls(tool=tool, ok=True, data=data, source=source, warnings=list(warnings or []))

    @classmethod
    def failure(cls, tool, error, source="", warnings=None) -> "ToolResult":
        return cls(tool=tool, ok=False, error=str(error), source=source, warnings=list(warnings or []))

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

Writing schema.py

market_tools.py¶

In [5]:
%%writefile market_tools.py
"""Market specialist tools (yfinance). Never raise: always return a ToolResult.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (market_tools.py):
- No behavioral change. `ticker_factory` injection and missing-field handling kept as written.
- Header note added so the teammate can see the file was reviewed and left intact.
- Price and fundamental tools never raise. Missing fields become warnings or None
so the market and earnings specialists can still produce a cited section.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Any, Callable

from schema import ToolResult

SOURCE = "Yahoo Finance (yfinance)"
PRICE_COLS = ["Open", "High", "Low", "Close", "Volume"]

NUMERIC_FIELDS = {
    "market_cap": "marketCap",
    "trailing_pe": "trailingPE",
    "forward_pe": "forwardPE",
    "trailing_eps": "trailingEps",
    "forward_eps": "forwardEps",
    "dividend_yield": "dividendYield",
    "beta": "beta",
    "revenue_growth": "revenueGrowth",
    "profit_margin": "profitMargins",
    "fifty_two_week_high": "fiftyTwoWeekHigh",
    "fifty_two_week_low": "fiftyTwoWeekLow",
}
TEXT_FIELDS = {"name": "shortName", "sector": "sector", "industry": "industry", "currency": "currency"}


def _default_factory(symbol: str):
    import yfinance as yf  # lazy import so tests don't need the package

    return yf.Ticker(symbol)


def _num(value: Any) -> float | None:
    """Coerce to a finite float, or None (handles None, NaN, 'N/A', inf)."""
    try:
        f = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return None if math.isnan(f) or math.isinf(f) else f


def _round(v: float | None, n: int = 4) -> float | None:
    return None if v is None else round(v, n)


def get_price_history(ticker: str, period: str = "6mo", interval: str = "1d",
                      ticker_factory: Callable | None = None) -> ToolResult:
    tool, sym = "get_price_history", ticker.upper().strip()
    try:
        df = (ticker_factory or _default_factory)(sym).history(period=period, interval=interval)
    except Exception as exc:  # network, bad ticker, yfinance internals
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", SOURCE)
    if df is None or len(df) == 0:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"No price rows for '{sym}' (bad ticker or no data)", SOURCE)

    warnings: list[str] = []
    df = df.copy()
    for col in PRICE_COLS:
        if col not in df.columns:
            warnings.append(f"Column {col} missing from provider response")
            df[col] = float("nan")
    df = df.dropna(subset=["Close"])
    if df.empty:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, "All Close values were missing", SOURCE, warnings)
    if len(df) < 20:
        warnings.append(f"Only {len(df)} rows; moving averages/volatility may be unavailable")

    close = df["Close"].astype(float)
    n = len(close)
    last, first = float(close.iloc[-1]), float(close.iloc[0])
    daily = close.pct_change().dropna()

    metrics = {
        "rows": n,
        "start_date": str(df.index[0])[:10],
        "end_date": str(df.index[-1])[:10],
        "last_close": _round(last),
        "period_return_pct": _round((last / first - 1) * 100 if first else None, 2),
        "return_1m_pct": _round((last / float(close.iloc[-22]) - 1) * 100, 2) if n > 22 else None,
        "period_high": _round(_num(df["High"].max())),
        "period_low": _round(_num(df["Low"].min())),
        "avg_volume": _round(_num(df["Volume"].mean()), 0),
        "sma_20": _round(float(close.tail(20).mean())) if n >= 20 else None,
        "sma_50": _round(float(close.tail(50).mean())) if n >= 50 else None,
        "annualized_vol_pct": _round(float(daily.std() * math.sqrt(252) * 100), 2) if len(daily) >= 2 else None,
    }
    history = [
        {"date": str(idx)[:10], **{c.lower(): _round(_num(row[c])) for c in PRICE_COLS}}
        for idx, row in df.iterrows()
    ]
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"ticker": sym, "metrics": metrics, "history": history}, SOURCE, warnings)


def get_fundamentals(ticker: str, ticker_factory: Callable | None = None) -> ToolResult:
    tool, sym = "get_fundamentals", ticker.upper().strip()
    try:
        t = (ticker_factory or _default_factory)(sym)
        info = t.info or {}
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", SOURCE)

    fields = {k: _num(info.get(src)) for k, src in NUMERIC_FIELDS.items()}
    fields.update({k: (info.get(src) or None) for k, src in TEXT_FIELDS.items()})
    missing = [k for k, v in fields.items() if v is None]

    # Earnings date is optional: only report it if the provider has it.
    try:
        cal = getattr(t, "calendar", None)
        dates = cal.get("Earnings Date") if isinstance(cal, dict) else None
        fields["next_earnings_date"] = str(dates[0]) if dates else None
    except Exception:
        fields["next_earnings_date"] = None
    if fields["next_earnings_date"] is None:
        missing.append("next_earnings_date")

    if all(fields[k] is None for k in NUMERIC_FIELDS):
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"No fundamentals returned for '{sym}'", SOURCE,
                                  [f"Missing: {', '.join(missing)}"])
    warnings = [f"Missing fields: {', '.join(missing)}"] if missing else []
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"ticker": sym, "fields": fields, "missing": missing}, SOURCE, warnings)


def to_memory_metrics(price: ToolResult | None, fundamentals: ToolResult | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Flatten the numbers worth remembering between runs."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if price and price.ok:
        m = price.data["metrics"]
        out.update({k: m.get(k) for k in ("last_close", "period_return_pct", "return_1m_pct",
                                          "sma_20", "sma_50", "annualized_vol_pct", "end_date")})
    if fundamentals and fundamentals.ok:
        f = fundamentals.data["fields"]
        out.update({k: f.get(k) for k in ("market_cap", "trailing_pe", "forward_pe", "trailing_eps")})
    return out

In [6]:
%%writefile news_tools.py
"""News tools: NewsAPI (live), Yahoo Finance headlines, or a headline dump.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (news_tools.py) and vs the News_Ingestion_Pipeline notebook:
- ADDED fetch_yahoo_news(). Original agent only called NewsAPI. Yahoo needs no key and is the
  source the news notebook already used. Empty Yahoo responses now return ToolResult.failure.
- ADDED article-level category tagging with the same keyword families as chain.py, so the router
  still has a destination. The news notebook's binary earnings/general_noise label is mapped:
  earnings stays earnings; general_noise becomes other.
- ADDED published_at. The news notebook dropped Yahoo's pubDate.
- REMOVED the synthetic fallback article ("record quarterly revenue of $85.8 billion"). That text
  was indexed with a fake URL and a hardcoded 0.98 confidence. It must never enter the index or
  the analyst note. An empty fetch is a data gap.
- Tightened NewsAPI query to ticker + financial keywords.
- Added _is_financially_relevant post-filter so general-web noise never reaches the chain.
- NewsAPI path (fetch_news_newsapi, load_headline_dump, _clean, _dedupe) kept as written.
- The financial keyword filter is generic (no company names). It reduces
  general-web noise before the chain sees the articles, while the safety
  gate in preprocess still prevents an empty news set.
- Order of sources: NewsAPI first when NEWSAPI_KEY is set and it returns rows; Yahoo otherwise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import re
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Callable

from schema import ToolResult

MAX_BODY = 500
SOURCE_NEWSAPI = "NewsAPI"
SOURCE_YAHOO = "Yahoo Finance news (yfinance)"

# CHANGE: financial relevance filter so general-web noise does not reach the chain.
# Keeps an article only if the title/body contains a financial keyword.
# Why: the original news pull included irrelevant articles that only contained the ticker.
FINANCIAL_KEYWORDS = (
    "earnings", "eps", "revenue", "guidance", "quarter", "profit", "results",
    "upgrade", "downgrade", "price target", "analyst", "rating", "outperform",
    "underperform", "lawsuit", "antitrust", "regulator", "sec", "doj", "ftc",
    "acquire", "acquisition", "merger", "buyout", "stake", "takeover",
    "fed", "rate", "inflation", "tariff", "gdp", "recession", "cpi",
    "dividend", "buyback", "ceo", "cfo", "outlook", "forecast",
    "subscribers", "margin", "operating", "cash flow", "debt",
)


def _is_financially_relevant(title: str, body: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the article text contains any financial keyword.

    Generic: no company-specific terms, so it works for any ticker.
    """
    text = f"{title} {body}".lower()
    return any(kw in text for kw in FINANCIAL_KEYWORDS)


# Same families as chain.py KEYWORDS, so a pre-tag does not fight the chain.
CATEGORY_PATTERNS = {
    "earnings": [r"\bearnings\b", r"\beps\b", r"\brevenue\b", r"\bguidance\b", r"\bquarter\b", r"\bprofit\b"],
    "analyst_rating": [r"\bupgrade\b", r"\bdowngrade\b", r"\bprice target\b", r"\banalyst\b", r"\boutperform\b"],
    "legal_regulatory": [r"\blawsuit\b", r"\bantitrust\b", r"\bregulator\b", r"\bsec\b", r"\bdoj\b", r"\bftc\b"],
    "m_and_a": [r"\bacquir\w*", r"\bmerger\b", r"\bbuyout\b", r"\btakeover\b", r"\bstake\b"],
    "macro": [r"\bfed\b", r"\brate cut\b", r"\binflation\b", r"\btariff\b", r"\bgdp\b", r"\brecession\b"],
    "product": [r"\blaunch\b", r"\bunveil\b", r"\brelease\b", r"\bnew product\b", r"\bfeature\b"],
}


def _default_get(url: str) -> dict:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())


def _clean(a: dict) -> dict:
    src = a.get("source")
    return {
        "title": (a.get("title") or "").strip(),
        "body": (a.get("description") or a.get("body") or a.get("content") or "")[:MAX_BODY],
        "source": (src.get("name") if isinstance(src, dict) else src) or "unknown",
        "published_at": a.get("publishedAt") or a.get("published_at") or a.get("timestamp") or "",
        "url": a.get("url") or "",
    }


def _dedupe(items: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    seen, out = set(), []
    for it in items:
        key = it["title"].lower()
        if it["title"] and key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            out.append(it)
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: x["published_at"], reverse=True)


def tag_category(title: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Rule category for one article. Returns one of chain.py's CATEGORIES."""
    text = f"{title} {body}".lower()
    for cat, pats in CATEGORY_PATTERNS.items():
        if any(re.search(p, text) for p in pats):
            return cat
    return "other"  # news notebook called this general_noise; agent router expects other


def _stamp(article: dict) -> dict:
    """Attach category without dropping fields the chain reads."""
    out = dict(article)
    out["category"] = tag_category(out.get("title", ""), out.get("body", ""))
    return out


def fetch_news_newsapi(query: str, api_key: str | None, days: int = 14, limit: int = 30,
                       http_get: Callable[[str], dict] | None = None) -> ToolResult:
    """NewsAPI fetch with a generic financial query and post-filter.

    CHANGE: query is now (ticker) AND (financial terms). Works for any symbol.
    Articles that fail the financial keyword check are dropped before return.
    """
    tool, src = "fetch_news", SOURCE_NEWSAPI
    if not api_key and http_get is None:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, "NEWSAPI_KEY not set", src)
    since = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=days)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    # Generic financial query — no company name or sector is hardcoded.
    financial_q = (
        f'({query}) AND (earnings OR revenue OR guidance OR "price target" OR analyst '
        f'OR dividend OR buyback OR lawsuit OR merger OR acquisition OR outlook OR forecast '
        f'OR "operating margin" OR "cash flow")'
    )
    qs = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "q": financial_q, "from": since, "language": "en",
        "sortBy": "publishedAt", "pageSize": limit, "apiKey": api_key or "",
    })
    try:
        payload = (http_get or _default_get)(f"https://newsapi.org/v2/everything?{qs}")
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", src)
    if payload.get("status") not in (None, "ok"):
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, payload.get("message", "NewsAPI error"), src)
    cleaned = [_stamp(a) for a in _dedupe([_clean(a) for a in payload.get("articles", [])])]
    # Drop non-financial articles.
    items = [a for a in cleaned if _is_financially_relevant(a.get("title", ""), a.get("body", ""))]
    warnings = [] if items else ["No financially relevant articles returned"]
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"query": financial_q, "count": len(items), "articles": items}, src, warnings)


def load_headline_dump(path: str) -> ToolResult:
    tool, src = "fetch_news", f"headline dump: {path}"
    try:
        if path.lower().endswith(".csv"):
            with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                raw = list(csv.DictReader(f))
        else:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                raw = json.load(f)
            raw = raw.get("articles", raw) if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", src)
    items = [_stamp(a) for a in _dedupe([_clean(a) for a in raw])]
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"query": "dump", "count": len(items), "articles": items}, src,
                              [] if items else ["Dump contained no articles"])


def _yahoo_time(item: dict, content: dict) -> str:
    """Normalize Yahoo's several date shapes to an ISO-like string. Original news notebook dropped this."""
    for key in ("pubDate", "displayTime", "providerPublishTime"):
        raw = content.get(key) or item.get(key)
        if not raw:
            continue
        if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(raw, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        return str(raw)
    return ""


def fetch_yahoo_news(ticker: str) -> ToolResult:
    """Yahoo headlines for one ticker. No API key. Empty result is a failure, not a fake article.

    CHANGE: this function did not exist in Deepika's news_tools.py. It replaces the news notebook's
    fetch_and_process_news, which injected a synthetic earnings paragraph when Yahoo returned [].
    """
    tool, sym = "fetch_news", ticker.upper().strip()
    try:
        import yfinance as yf  # lazy: tests that stub this function never import it
        raw = yf.Ticker(sym).news or []
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", SOURCE_YAHOO)
    articles = []
    for item in raw:
        content = item.get("content") if isinstance(item.get("content"), dict) else {}
        title = (content.get("title") or item.get("title") or "").strip()
        body = (content.get("summary") or content.get("description") or item.get("summary") or "")[:MAX_BODY]
        url = ""
        canon = content.get("canonicalUrl")
        if isinstance(canon, dict):
            url = canon.get("url") or ""
        url = url or item.get("link") or ""
        provider = content.get("provider") if isinstance(content.get("provider"), dict) else {}
        source = provider.get("displayName") or item.get("publisher") or "Yahoo Finance"
        if not title:
            continue
        articles.append(_stamp({
            "title": title, "body": body, "source": source,
            "published_at": _yahoo_time(item, content), "url": url,
        }))
    articles = _dedupe(articles)
    if not articles:
        # CHANGE: news notebook indexed a hardcoded $85.8B paragraph here. We refuse.
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"Yahoo returned 0 articles for '{sym}' (rate limit or empty feed)", SOURCE_YAHOO)
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"query": sym, "count": len(articles), "articles": articles}, SOURCE_YAHOO)


def fetch_news(ticker: str, query: str | None = None, api_key: str | None = None) -> ToolResult:
    """Wrapper used by the agent. NewsAPI if a key is set and it returns rows; otherwise Yahoo.

    No company name, sector, or other ticker-specific string is hardcoded. `query` defaults to the ticker.
    """
    key = api_key if api_key is not None else os.getenv("NEWSAPI_KEY")
    q = query or ticker
    if key:
        live = fetch_news_newsapi(q, key)
        if live.ok and live.data.get("count", 0) > 0:
            return live
        yahoo = fetch_yahoo_news(ticker)
        if yahoo.ok:
            yahoo.warnings = list(yahoo.warnings) + [f"NewsAPI empty or failed ({live.error}); used Yahoo"]
            return yahoo
        return live if not live.ok else yahoo
    return fetch_yahoo_news(ticker)

%%writefile extra_tools.py
"""Optional data tools: FRED (macro) and SEC EDGAR (filings).

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (extra_tools.py):
- No behavioral change. Header note added.
- SEC_USER_AGENT still read from the environment. Do not hardcode a personal email here.
- Optional macro and EDGAR tools. Failures are returned as ToolResult so
  the agent can note the gap without stopping the rest of the research.
"""
import json
import os
import urllib.request

from schema import ToolResult


def _get(url, headers=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers or {})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())


def _sec_get(url):
    ua = os.getenv("SEC_USER_AGENT", "AAI520 InvestmentResearchAgent student-project contact@example.com")
    return _get(url, {"User-Agent": ua})


def get_macro(series=("FEDFUNDS", "DGS10", "CPIAUCSL"), api_key=None, http_get=None):
    tool, src = "get_macro", "FRED"
    key = api_key or os.getenv("FRED_API_KEY")
    if not key and http_get is None:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, "FRED_API_KEY not set", src)
    out, warns = [], []
    for sid in series:
        url = (f"https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations?series_id={sid}"
               f"&api_key={key or ''}&file_type=json&sort_order=desc&limit=3")
        try:
            obs = (http_get or _get)(url).get("observations", [])
        except Exception as exc:
            warns.append(f"{sid}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            continue
        for o in obs:
            try:
                out.append({"id": sid, "date": o["date"], "value": float(o["value"])})
                break
            except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
                continue  # FRED uses "." for missing values
    if not out:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, "No FRED observations returned", src, warns)
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"series": out}, src, warns)


def get_edgar_filings(ticker, forms=("10-K", "10-Q", "8-K"), limit=5, http_get=None):
    tool, src = "get_edgar_filings", "SEC EDGAR"
    get = http_get or _sec_get
    try:
        table = get("https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json")
        row = next((v for v in table.values() if v.get("ticker", "").upper() == ticker.upper()), None)
        if not row:
            return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"Ticker {ticker} not found in SEC ticker table", src)
        cik = str(row["cik_str"]).zfill(10)
        recent = get(f"https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{cik}.json")["filings"]["recent"]
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolResult.failure(tool, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", src)
    filings = []
    for form, d, acc, doc in zip(recent["form"], recent["filingDate"], recent["accessionNumber"],
                                 recent["primaryDocument"]):
        if form in forms:
            filings.append({"form": form, "date": d,
                            "url": f"https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{int(cik)}/{acc.replace('-', '')}/{doc}"})
        if len(filings) >= limit:
            break
    warns = [] if filings else ["No matching recent filings"]
    return ToolResult.success(tool, {"company": row.get("title"), "cik": cik, "filings": filings}, src, warns)

%%writefile llm.py
"""LLM wrappers + tolerant JSON parsing.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (llm.py):
- ClaudeLLM default model changed from "claude-sonnet-5-5" (not a real model id) to
  "claude-sonnet-4-5". This notebook uses Gemini. Claude is only selected if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set.
- No other behavioral change. Wrappers still return "" on error so the agent falls back to rules.
- LLM calls are optional. On any error the wrapper returns empty so the
  agent falls back to the deterministic rule path and still emits a note.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import time


class ClaudeLLM:
    def __init__(self, model="claude-sonnet-4-5", max_tokens=1800):  # CHANGE: was "claude-sonnet-5-5"
        import anthropic

        self.client = anthropic.Anthropic()
        self.model, self.max_tokens, self.calls, self.last_error = model, max_tokens, 0, None

    def __call__(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
        self.calls += 1
        try:
            r = self.client.messages.create(model=self.model, max_tokens=self.max_tokens, system=system,
                                            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}])
            return "".join(b.text for b in r.content if b.type == "text")
        except Exception as exc:
            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            return ""


class GeminiLLM:
    """Google Gemini via the `google-genai` SDK (pip install google-genai).

    CHANGE (2026-10-17, Cameron):
    - Default model comes from the GEMINI_MODEL environment variable (fallback "gemini-3.8-flash").
    - max_tokens 4096 -> 8192. Thinking tokens count against max_output_tokens, so long notes
      were cut off mid-sentence.
    - A reply that stops with finish_reason MAX_TOKENS is counted in self.truncated and recorded in
      self.last_error, so the LLM status line shows it.
    - Optional thinking control: set GEMINI_THINKING_LEVEL (e.g. "low") or GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGET
      (e.g. "1024"). If the model rejects the setting, it is dropped and the call is retried.
    """

    def __init__(self, model=None, max_tokens=8192, api_key=None, retries=3):
        from google import genai
        from google.genai import types

        key = api_key or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY")
        if not key:
            raise ValueError("Set GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY)")
        self.client, self._types = genai.Client(api_key=key), types
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.8-flash")
        self.max_tokens, self.retries = max_tokens, retries
        self.calls, self.last_error, self.truncated = 0, None, 0
        self._thinking = self._thinking_config()

    def _thinking_config(self):
        """Optional ThinkingConfig from env vars; None (SDK default) when unset or invalid."""
        level, budget = os.getenv("GEMINI_THINKING_LEVEL"), os.getenv("GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGET")
        try:
            if level:
                return self._types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=level.upper())
            if budget:
                return self._types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=int(budget))
        except Exception as exc:  # bad value: keep the SDK default instead of failing
            self.last_error = f"thinking config ignored: {exc}"
        return None

    def _check_truncated(self, r):
        """Record replies that stopped because they hit max_output_tokens."""
        try:
            reason = r.candidates[0].finish_reason
        except (AttributeError, IndexError, TypeError):
            return
        if "MAX_TOKENS" in str(reason):
            self.truncated += 1
            self.last_error = (f"Truncated reply (finish_reason=MAX_TOKENS at max_output_tokens="
                               f"{self.max_tokens}) on call {self.calls}")

    def __call__(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
        self.calls += 1
        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
            extra = {"thinking_config": self._thinking} if self._thinking else {}
            cfg = self._types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=system,
                                                    max_output_tokens=self.max_tokens, **extra)
            try:
                r = self.client.models.generate_content(model=self.model, contents=user, config=cfg)
                text = r.text or ""  # None when the reply is blocked/empty
            except Exception as exc:
                self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
                if self._thinking is not None and "thinking" in self.last_error.lower():
                    self._thinking = None  # model rejected the thinking setting: retry without it
                    continue
                transient = any(x in self.last_error for x in ("429", "503", "UNAVAILABLE", "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"))
                if transient and attempt < self.retries:
                    time.sleep(5 * attempt)  # rate limits: back off and retry
                    continue
                return ""
            self._check_truncated(r)
            return text
        return ""


def make_llm(provider="auto"):
    """provider: 'gemini' | 'claude' | 'auto' (Gemini first if its key is set). Returns None if no key."""
    if provider in ("gemini", "auto") and (os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY")):
        return GeminiLLM()
    if provider in ("claude", "auto") and os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        return ClaudeLLM()
    return None


def parse_json(text):
    """Extract the first JSON object/array from an LLM reply (handles ``` fences). None on failure."""
    if not text:
        return None
    text = re.sub(r"```(?:json)?", "", text)
    starts = [(text.find(o), c) for o, c in (("{", "}"), ("[", "]")) if text.find(o) != -1]
    for i, closer in sorted(starts):
        j = text.rfind(closer)
        if j > i:
            try:
                return json.loads(text[i:j + 1])
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pass
    return None

%%writefile memory.py
"""Enduring memory: past runs + LESSONS the agent learned. Stored as JSON keyed by ticker.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (memory.py):
- No behavioral change. Header note added. Path is still injected by the caller so Colab can
  point it at Google Drive.
- MemoryStore is the only state that survives between runs. It stores prior metrics and
  short lessons so the second run can show “Changes since last run” instead of “No prior run.”
"""
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def _now():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


class MemoryStore:
    def __init__(self, path="memory/store.json"):
        self.path = path
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or ".", exist_ok=True)

    def _load(self):
        try:
            with open(self.path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return {}

    def _save(self, db):
        tmp = self.path + ".tmp"
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(db, f, indent=2)
        os.replace(tmp, self.path)

    def _entry(self, db, ticker):
        e = db.setdefault(ticker.upper(), {})
        e.setdefault("runs", [])
        e.setdefault("lessons", [])
        return e

    def last_run(self, ticker):
        runs = self._load().get(ticker.upper(), {}).get("runs", [])
        return runs[-1] if runs else None

    def save_run(self, ticker, run_id, metrics, headlines, critique, brief, scores=None):
        db = self._load()
        e = self._entry(db, ticker)
        e["runs"].append({"run_id": run_id, "saved_at": _now(), "metrics": metrics,
                          "headlines": headlines[:15], "critique": critique, "scores": scores or {},
                          "brief": brief})
        e["runs"] = e["runs"][-20:]
        self._save(db)

    @staticmethod
    def diff(prev, current):
        if not prev:
            return []
        out = []
        for k, new in current.items():
            old = prev.get("metrics", {}).get(k)
            if isinstance(new, (int, float)) and isinstance(old, (int, float)) and old != new:
                pct = f" ({(new / old - 1) * 100:+.1f}%)" if old else ""
                out.append(f"{k}: {old} -> {new}{pct}")
        return out

    def get_lessons(self, ticker):
        return self._load().get(ticker.upper(), {}).get("lessons", [])

    def update_lessons(self, ticker, rule_lessons, llm_lessons):
        """Rule-based lessons are REPLACED each run; LLM lessons accumulate (max 5 newest).

        CHANGE (2026-10-17): the saved list is de-duplicated by (tag, text), keeping the first
        occurrence and its order. A tool that fails twice (e.g. fetch_news, then the widened
        re-query) used to save the same rule lesson twice.
        """
        db = self._load()
        e = self._entry(db, ticker)
        kept_llm = [l for l in e["lessons"] if l.get("source") == "llm"]
        new_llm = [{"tag": "llm", "text": t, "source": "llm", "updated": _now()} for t in llm_lessons]
        seen, merged = set(), []
        for l in new_llm + kept_llm:
            if l["text"] not in seen:
                seen.add(l["text"])
                merged.append(l)
        rules = [{**l, "source": "rules", "updated": _now()} for l in rule_lessons]
        unique, keys = [], set()
        for lesson in rules + merged[:5]:  # order-preserving de-duplication
            key = (lesson.get("tag"), lesson.get("text"))
            if key not in keys:
                keys.add(key)
                unique.append(lesson)
        e["lessons"] = unique
        self._save(db)
        return e["lessons"]

%%writefile chain.py
"""WORKFLOW PATTERN 1 - PROMPT CHAINING
Ingest -> Preprocess -> Classify -> Extract -> Summarize

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (chain.py):
- BEHAVIOR CHANGE (Cameron, 2026-10-12): preprocess now requires both a ticker/company
  mention AND a financial keyword before an article counts as relevant. Generic keyword
  list (no company-specific terms). The safety gate is preserved: if fewer than 3 articles
  pass, the unfiltered set is used, so the chain never receives an empty article list.
- Classify, extract, and summarize gates and their rule fallbacks are unchanged.
- Category set is unchanged, so news_tools.tag_category can pre-label without fighting
  this module.

Why: prompt chaining splits news handling into small checked steps. Each stage has a gate
(LLM output must parse and use known labels or real article ids, else rules are used) and
writes to stage_log, so the notebook output shows the chain executed.
"""

import html
import json
import re
from collections import Counter

from llm import parse_json

CATEGORIES = ["earnings", "product", "legal_regulatory", "macro", "analyst_rating", "m_and_a", "other"]
SENTIMENTS = ["positive", "neutral", "negative"]
KEYWORDS = {
    "earnings": ["earnings", "eps", "revenue", "guidance", "quarter", "quarterly", "profit", "results"],
    "analyst_rating": ["upgrade", "downgrade", "price target", "analyst", "rating", "outperform", "underperform"],
    "legal_regulatory": ["lawsuit", "sues", "antitrust", "regulator", "regulatory", "fine", "sec", "doj", "ftc", "probe", "court"],
    "m_and_a": ["acquire", "acquisition", "merger", "buyout", "stake", "takeover"],
    "macro": ["fed", "rate cut", "rate hike", "inflation", "tariff", "tariffs", "gdp", "recession", "cpi"],
    "product": ["launch", "unveil", "release", "announces", "new product", "feature", "rollout"],
}
POS = ["beat", "surge", "record", "growth", "upgrade", "gain", "rally", "strong", "raises", "soar", "profit", "outperform"]
NEG = ["miss", "fall", "drop", "lawsuit", "downgrade", "cut", "weak", "plunge", "probe", "fine", "decline",
       "slump", "concern", "risk", "underperform", "ban"]

CLASSIFY_SYSTEM = (
    "You classify financial news. For each article return the category "
    f"(one of {CATEGORIES}) and the sentiment for the stock (one of {SENTIMENTS}). "
    'Return JSON only: [{"id":"N1","category":"...","sentiment":"..."}]')
EXTRACT_SYSTEM = (
    "You extract facts from financial news. For each article give up to 3 concrete facts (events, figures, "
    'dates) copied from the text. Return JSON only: [{"id":"N1","facts":["..."],"numbers":["..."]}]')
SUMMARY_SYSTEM = (
    "You write news summaries for an equity analyst. Using ONLY the provided classified facts, write 3-4 "
    "sentences. Put the article id in brackets, like [N3], after every claim. Return plain text.")


def _has(text, kw):
    pat = rf"\b{re.escape(kw)}\w*" if len(kw) >= 5 else rf"\b{re.escape(kw)}\b"
    return re.search(pat, text) is not None


def _clean(s):
    s = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s or ""))
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def ingest(news_results):
    arts, errors = [], []
    for r in news_results:
        if r.ok:
            arts += r.data.get("articles", [])
        else:
            errors.append(f"{r.source or r.tool}: {r.error}")
    return arts, errors


def preprocess(articles, ticker, company=None, max_articles=30):
    """Deduplicate and apply a generic financial relevance gate.

    CHANGE: An article is kept as "relevant" only if it mentions the ticker
    (or company name) AND contains at least one financial keyword. Pure
    general-web noise is dropped. The original safety gate is preserved:
    if fewer than 3 articles pass the filter, the unfiltered set is used
    so the chain never receives an empty list.
    """
    names = [ticker.lower()] + ([company.lower().split()[0]] if company else [])
    # Generic financial keywords — works for any ticker.
    fin_kws = (
        "earnings", "eps", "revenue", "guidance", "quarter", "profit", "results",
        "analyst", "upgrade", "downgrade", "price target", "rating", "outperform",
        "lawsuit", "antitrust", "regulator", "sec", "merger", "acquisition",
        "buyout", "dividend", "buyback", "outlook", "forecast", "margin",
        "subscribers", "cash flow", "debt", "ceo", "cfo",
    )
    seen, out = set(), []
    for a in articles:
        title, body = _clean(a.get("title")), _clean(a.get("body"))
        key = re.sub(r"\W+", "", title.lower())
        if not title or key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        text = f"{title} {body}".lower()
        has_name = any(_has(text, n) for n in names)
        has_fin = any(kw in text for kw in fin_kws)
        out.append({
            "title": title,
            "body": body[:400],
            "source": a.get("source") or "unknown",
            "published_at": a.get("published_at", ""),
            "url": a.get("url", ""),
            "relevant": has_name and has_fin,  # both signals required
        })
    relevant = [a for a in out if a["relevant"]]
    # Safety gate (unchanged): never filter down to nothing.
    kept = (relevant if len(relevant) >= 3 else out)[:max_articles]
    for i, a in enumerate(kept, 1):
        a["id"] = f"N{i}"
    return kept, {
        "in": len(articles),
        "after_dedupe": len(out),
        "kept": len(kept),
        "financially_relevant": len(relevant),
    }


def _rule_classify(a):
    text = f"{a['title']} {a['body']}".lower()
    hits = {c: sum(_has(text, k) for k in kws) for c, kws in KEYWORDS.items()}
    cat = max(hits, key=hits.get) if any(hits.values()) else "other"
    score = sum(_has(text, w) for w in POS) - sum(_has(text, w) for w in NEG)
    return cat, ("positive" if score > 0 else "negative" if score < 0 else "neutral")


def classify(articles, llm=None):
    labels = {}
    if llm:
        payload = [{"id": a["id"], "title": a["title"], "body": a["body"][:200]} for a in articles]
        data = parse_json(llm(CLASSIFY_SYSTEM, json.dumps(payload)))
        if isinstance(data, list):
            labels = {d.get("id"): d for d in data if isinstance(d, dict)}
    for a in articles:
        p = labels.get(a["id"], {})
        if p.get("category") in CATEGORIES and p.get("sentiment") in SENTIMENTS:  # GATE
            a["category"], a["sentiment"], a["label_source"] = p["category"], p["sentiment"], "llm"
        else:
            a["category"], a["sentiment"] = _rule_classify(a)
            a["label_source"] = "rules"
    return articles


NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\$?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?\s?(?:%|percent|billion|million|trillion|bn)?", re.I)


def extract(articles, llm=None):
    parsed = {}
    if llm:
        payload = [{"id": a["id"], "title": a["title"], "body": a["body"]} for a in articles]
        data = parse_json(llm(EXTRACT_SYSTEM, json.dumps(payload)))
        if isinstance(data, list):
            parsed = {d.get("id"): d for d in data if isinstance(d, dict)}
    for a in articles:
        d = parsed.get(a["id"], {})
        facts = [str(x)[:200] for x in d["facts"] if isinstance(x, str)][:3] if isinstance(d.get("facts"), list) else []
        nums = [str(x)[:40] for x in d["numbers"] if isinstance(x, (str, int, float))][:5] if isinstance(d.get("numbers"), list) else []
        if facts:  # GATE: need at least one fact
            a["extract_source"] = "llm"
        else:
            facts = [a["title"]]
            nums = [n.strip() for n in NUM_RE.findall(f"{a['title']} {a['body']}") if len(n.strip()) >= 2][:5]
            a["extract_source"] = "rules"
        a["facts"], a["numbers"] = facts, nums
    return articles


def summarize(articles, llm=None):
    sc = Counter(a["sentiment"] for a in articles)
    cc = Counter(a["category"] for a in articles)
    top = sorted(articles, key=lambda a: a["sentiment"] == "neutral")[:3]
    themes = ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in cc.most_common(3))
    notable = "; ".join(f"{a['title']} [{a['id']}]" for a in top)
    text = (f"{len(articles)} relevant articles: {sc['positive']} positive, {sc['neutral']} neutral, "
            f"{sc['negative']} negative. Main themes: {themes}. Notable: {notable}")
    src = "rules"
    if llm:
        payload = [{"id": a["id"], "category": a["category"], "sentiment": a["sentiment"], "facts": a["facts"]}
                   for a in articles[:15]]
        out = (llm(SUMMARY_SYSTEM, json.dumps(payload)) or "").strip()
        # FIX (2026-10-17): also accept combined citations like [N1, N3]; the old pattern only
        # matched [N1], so a valid LLM summary using the combined form fell back to rules.
        groups = re.findall(r"\[\s*(N\d+(?:\s*[,;]\s*N\d+)*)\s*\]", out)
        cited = {i for grp in groups for i in re.split(r"\s*[,;]\s*", grp)}
        if out and cited and cited <= {a["id"] for a in articles}:  # GATE: must cite real articles
            text, src = out, "llm"
    return {"summary": text, "summary_source": src, "sentiment_counts": dict(sc), "category_counts": dict(cc)}


def run_news_chain(news_results, ticker, company=None, llm=None):
    log = []
    arts, errors = ingest(news_results)
    log.append({"stage": "ingest", "articles": len(arts), "errors": errors})
    arts, pstats = preprocess(arts, ticker, company)
    log.append({"stage": "preprocess", **pstats})
    if not arts:
        return {"articles": [], "summary": "No usable news articles were retrieved.", "sentiment_counts": {},
                "category_counts": {}, "stage_log": log, "errors": errors}
    arts = classify(arts, llm)
    log.append({"stage": "classify", "by_llm": sum(a["label_source"] == "llm" for a in arts),
                "by_rules": sum(a["label_source"] == "rules" for a in arts)})
    arts = extract(arts, llm)
    log.append({"stage": "extract", "by_llm": sum(a["extract_source"] == "llm" for a in arts),
                "by_rules": sum(a["extract_source"] == "rules" for a in arts)})
    digest = summarize(arts, llm)
    log.append({"stage": "summarize", "source": digest["summary_source"]})
    return {"articles": arts, **digest, "stage_log": log, "errors": errors}

%%writefile router.py
"""WORKFLOW PATTERN 2 - ROUTING

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (router.py, MarketSpecialist.analyze):
- BUG FIX. Original set pos = "between" and interpolated it as
  "trading {pos} of its 20/50-day averages" and "price is {pos} of them".
  That printed "trading between of its 20/50-day averages" in the saved AAPL note.
  pos is now a complete phrase: "above both averages", "below both averages",
  "between the two averages". The risk check still keys off the below-both case.
- BUG FIX (2026-10-17, NewsSpecialist.analyze). ARTICLE_ROUTES sends earnings and
  analyst_rating articles to the Earnings specialist, so the News specialist's bucket can
  be empty even when the chain found articles. It used to print "No news retrieved." in the
  Summary while the News section listed articles. It now checks the full chain digest.
- No other routing change. Tool and article routes are unchanged.

Why: routing sends each tool result or article to the specialist that knows how to read it
(market, earnings, or news), so each section of the note is written from the right evidence.
"""

from datetime import date

TOOL_ROUTES = {"get_price_history": "market", "get_macro": "market",
               "get_fundamentals": "earnings", "get_edgar_filings": "earnings"}
ARTICLE_ROUTES = {"earnings": "earnings", "analyst_rating": "earnings"}  # everything else -> news


def _cite(*ids):
    return " " + "".join(f"[{i}]" for i in ids)


def _fmt(v, nd=2, suf=""):
    return "n/a" if v is None else f"{v:.{nd}f}{suf}"


def _fmt_big(v):
    if v is None:
        return "n/a"
    for div, suf in ((1e12, "T"), (1e9, "B"), (1e6, "M")):
        if abs(v) >= div:
            return f"${v / div:.2f}{suf}"
    return f"${v:,.0f}"


def _find(items, tool):
    return next((i for i in items if i["kind"] == "tool" and i["tool"] == tool and i["result"].ok), None)


def _days_until(datestr, today):
    try:
        return (date.fromisoformat(str(datestr)[:10]) - date.fromisoformat(today)).days
    except Exception:
        return None


class Router:
    def route(self, items):
        buckets, log = {"market": [], "earnings": [], "news": []}, []
        for it in items:
            if it["kind"] == "tool":
                dest, why = TOOL_ROUTES.get(it["tool"]), f"tool '{it['tool']}'"
            else:
                cat = it["article"]["category"]
                dest, why = ARTICLE_ROUTES.get(cat, "news"), f"article category '{cat}'"
            if dest is None:
                log.append({"item": it["sid"], "to": None, "why": why + " has no specialist"})
                continue
            buckets[dest].append(it)
            log.append({"item": it["sid"], "to": dest, "why": why})
        return buckets, log


class MarketSpecialist:
    def analyze(self, items, ctx):
        out = {"headline": "Market data unavailable.", "findings": [], "risks": []}
        price, macro = _find(items, "get_price_history"), _find(items, "get_macro")
        if price:
            m, c = price["result"].data["metrics"], _cite(price["sid"])
            last, s20, s50 = m["last_close"], m.get("sma_20"), m.get("sma_50")
            # CHANGE (Deepika original used pos="between", which produced "between of").
            pos = None
            if s20 and s50:
                if last > s20 and last > s50:
                    pos = "above both averages"
                elif last < s20 and last < s50:
                    pos = "below both averages"
                else:
                    pos = "between the two averages"
            hi, lo = m.get("period_high"), m.get("period_low")
            rng = (last - lo) / (hi - lo) * 100 if hi and lo and hi > lo else None
            out["findings"] = [
                f"Last close {last} on {m['end_date']}{c}",
                f"Return {_fmt(m['period_return_pct'], 1, '%')} over {m['rows']} sessions; last month {_fmt(m.get('return_1m_pct'), 1, '%')}{c}",
                f"20-day average {_fmt(s20)} and 50-day average {_fmt(s50)}; price is {pos or 'n/a'}{c}",
                f"Sits at {_fmt(rng, 0, '%')} of its period range ({lo} to {hi}){c}",
                f"Annualized volatility {_fmt(m.get('annualized_vol_pct'), 1, '%')}{c}",
            ]
            out["headline"] = (f"{ctx['ticker']} closed at {last}, {_fmt(m['period_return_pct'], 1, '%')} over "
                               f"{m['rows']} sessions, trading {pos or 'n/a'}{c}")
            vol = m.get("annualized_vol_pct")
            if vol and vol > 35:
                out["risks"].append(f"Elevated volatility ({vol:.1f}% annualized){c}")
            if pos == "below both averages":  # CHANGE: was pos == "below both"
                out["risks"].append(f"Price is below its 20- and 50-day averages (weak trend){c}")
            if rng is not None and rng > 90:
                out["risks"].append(f"Trading near the top of its period range ({rng:.0f}%), limited cushion{c}")
        if macro:
            c = _cite(macro["sid"])
            for s in macro["result"].data["series"]:
                out["findings"].append(f"Macro: {s['id']} = {s['value']} ({s['date']}){c}")
        return out


class EarningsSpecialist:
    def analyze(self, items, ctx):
        out = {"headline": "Fundamentals unavailable.", "findings": [], "risks": []}
        fund, edgar = _find(items, "get_fundamentals"), _find(items, "get_edgar_filings")
        if fund:
            f, c = fund["result"].data["fields"], _cite(fund["sid"])
            tpe, fpe = f.get("trailing_pe"), f.get("forward_pe")
            out["findings"] += [
                f"{f.get('name') or ctx['ticker']} ({f.get('sector') or 'sector n/a'}), market cap {_fmt_big(f.get('market_cap'))}{c}",
                f"Trailing P/E {_fmt(tpe, 1)}, forward P/E {_fmt(fpe, 1)}, trailing EPS {_fmt(f.get('trailing_eps'))}{c}"]
            if tpe and fpe:
                out["findings"].append(("Forward P/E below trailing implies expected earnings growth" if fpe < tpe
                                        else "Forward P/E above trailing implies expected earnings decline") + c)
            days = _days_until(f.get("next_earnings_date"), ctx["run_date"])
            if f.get("next_earnings_date"):
                out["findings"].append(f"Next earnings {str(f['next_earnings_date'])[:10]}"
                                       + (f" (in {days} days)" if days is not None else "") + c)
            if days is not None and 0 <= days <= 14:
                out["risks"].append(f"Earnings in {days} days: event risk{c}")
            if tpe and tpe > 30:
                out["risks"].append(f"Premium valuation (trailing P/E {tpe:.1f}) leaves less room for disappointment{c}")
            out["headline"] = (f"Valued at {_fmt(tpe, 1)}x trailing earnings ({_fmt(fpe, 1)}x forward); "
                               f"next earnings {str(f.get('next_earnings_date') or 'n/a')[:10]}{c}")
        if edgar:
            fl = edgar["result"].data["filings"]
            out["findings"].append("Recent filings: " + "; ".join(f"{x['form']} {x['date']}" for x in fl[:4])
                                   + _cite(edgar["sid"]))
        for it in items:
            if it["kind"] == "article":
                a, c = it["article"], _cite(it["sid"])
                out["findings"].append(f"{a['category'].replace('_', ' ').title()} ({a['sentiment']}): {a['title']}{c}")
                if a["sentiment"] == "negative":
                    out["risks"].append(f"Negative earnings/analyst news: {a['title']}{c}")
        return out


class NewsSpecialist:
    def analyze(self, items, ctx):
        arts = [i for i in items if i["kind"] == "article"]
        out = {"headline": "", "findings": [], "risks": []}  # empty default
        if not arts:
            # FIX (2026-10-17): the router sends earnings/analyst articles to the
            # Earnings specialist, so an empty news bucket does not mean the chain
            # found no news. Check the full chain digest before saying "No news retrieved."
            n_all = len(ctx.get("digest", {}).get("articles", []))
            if n_all:
                out["headline"] = (f"All {n_all} relevant articles were earnings or "
                                   "analyst items; see Earnings & Fundamentals")
            else:
                out["headline"] = "No news retrieved."
            return out
        pos = sum(i["article"]["sentiment"] == "positive" for i in arts)
        neg = sum(i["article"]["sentiment"] == "negative" for i in arts)
        tone = "positive" if pos > neg else "negative" if neg > pos else "mixed"
        ids = [i["sid"] for i in arts[:3]]
        out["headline"] = f"Non-earnings news tone is {tone} ({pos} positive vs {neg} negative of {len(arts)})" + _cite(*ids)
        for it in arts[:5]:
            a, c = it["article"], _cite(it["sid"])
            out["findings"].append(f"{a['title']} ({a['source']}, {a['sentiment']}){c}")
            if a["sentiment"] == "negative":
                out["risks"].append(f"Negative headline: {a['title']}{c}")
        return out


SPECIALISTS = {"market": MarketSpecialist(), "earnings": EarningsSpecialist(), "news": NewsSpecialist()}


def run_specialists(buckets, ctx):
    return {name: SPECIALISTS[name].analyze(items, ctx) for name, items in buckets.items()}

%%writefile evaluator.py
"""WORKFLOW PATTERN 3 - EVALUATOR-OPTIMIZER

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (evaluator.py):
- Rubric, gates, and the offline section-inserter kept as written.
- Header note added.
- Evaluator–optimizer workflow: score the draft on grounding, completeness, balance,
  transparency, and memory use, then refine until the threshold is met or the refinement limit is reached.
- FIX (2026-10-17): sections() only recognised lines starting with exactly "## " and kept bold/
  numbering in the key, so LLM drafts using "### Summary", "**Summary**", "# Summary",
  "## **Summary:**" or "## 1. Summary" scored completeness 1 ("Missing sections: ...all 8").
  Headings are now normalised (any level 1-6, bold, numbering, trailing colon, case, spacing).
- FIX (2026-10-17): citations may be combined, e.g. "[S2, S3]". CITE_RE and cite_ids() accept
  that form for the grounding and unknown-id checks.
- ADDED (2026-10-17): an unclosed "[" marks a truncated note; completeness is capped at 2 so the
  optimizer refines it instead of passing a note cut off mid-sentence.
"""

import json
import re

from llm import parse_json

CRITERIA = ["grounding", "completeness", "balance", "transparency", "memory_use"]
NAME_MAP = {
    "summary": "Summary", "market": "Market", "earnings": "Earnings & Fundamentals", "news": "News",
    "changes since last run": "Changes since last run", "risks": "Risks & Open Questions",
    "data gaps": "Data gaps", "caveats": "Caveats"}
ORDER = list(NAME_MAP.values())
LEAN_SKIP = ("Risks & Open Questions", "Data gaps")  # first draft only writes sections with computed findings
# FIX: accept single "[S2]" and combined "[S2, S3]" / "[S2; N1]" citation forms.
CITE_RE = re.compile(r"\[\s*((?:S|N)\d+(?:\s*[,;]\s*(?:S|N)\d+)*)\s*\]")


def cite_ids(text):
    """Every [S#]/[N#] id in text, splitting combined brackets like [S2, S3] into S2 and S3."""
    return [i for grp in CITE_RE.findall(text) for i in re.split(r"\s*[,;]\s*", grp)]


WRITER_SYSTEM = (
    "You are an equity research analyst. Write a SHORT analyst note in Markdown using ONLY the evidence JSON. "
    "Use exactly these level-2 headings, in this order: ## Summary, ## Market, ## Earnings & Fundamentals, "
    "## News, ## Changes since last run, ## Risks & Open Questions, ## Data gaps, ## Caveats. "
    "Cite every figure with ids from valid_citation_ids, like [S2] or "
    "[N3]. Never invent ids. State missing data explicitly. No bare BUY/SELL rating. Apply lessons_from_past_runs. "
    # FIX (2026-10-17): point the writer at the prior-run lines compact() now sends, and keep the disclaimer.
    "Under ## Changes since last run, restate changes_since_last_run with its citation. "
    "End ## Caveats with: This is not investment advice.")
JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
    "You are a strict reviewer of analyst notes. Score 1-5 on: grounding (every number cited to real evidence), "
    "completeness, balance (risks stated), transparency (data gaps disclosed), memory_use (compares with prior run). "
    'Return JSON only: {"scores":{"grounding":5,...},"feedback":["specific fix", ...]}')
REFINE_SYSTEM = (
    "You revise analyst notes. Rewrite the note so that EVERY feedback item is fixed. Keep the same Markdown "
    "sections and [S#]/[N#] citations; use only the evidence provided; do not invent facts. Return the full note.")


def compact(ctx):
    """Evidence JSON sent to the LLM writer, judge, and refiner.

    FIX (2026-10-17): the writer only saw ctx["changes"], which is [] when no tracked metric moved,
    and never saw that a prior run existed. In Run 2 Gemini therefore wrote "memory contained no
    prior metrics". It now gets the same "Changes since last run" lines the rule path writes
    (including the [S#] memory citation) plus the prior run id.
    """
    return {"ticker": ctx["ticker"], "date": ctx["run_date"], "specialists": ctx["specialists"],
            "news_summary": ctx["digest"]["summary"], "gaps": ctx["gaps"],
            "changes_since_last_run": build_sections(ctx)["Changes since last run"],
            "prior_run_id": (ctx["prior"] or {}).get("run_id"),
            "lessons_from_past_runs": ctx["lessons"], "valid_citation_ids": ctx["valid_ids"],
            "sources": {k: {"tool": v["tool"], "source": v["source"], "fetched_at": v["fetched_at"]}
                        for k, v in ctx["sources"].items()}}


def _bullets(xs):
    return [f"- {x}" for x in xs]


def build_sections(ctx):
    sp = ctx["specialists"]
    cite = f" [{ctx['memory_sid']}]" if ctx.get("memory_sid") else ""
    if ctx["changes"]:
        changes = _bullets([c + cite for c in ctx["changes"]])
    elif ctx["prior"]:
        changes = [f"- No change in tracked metrics since run {ctx['prior']['run_id']}{cite}"]
    else:
        changes = ["- No prior run to compare."]
    risks = [r for k in ("market", "earnings", "news") for r in sp[k]["risks"]]
    return {
        "Summary": _bullets([sp[k]["headline"] for k in ("market", "earnings", "news")]),
        "Market": _bullets(sp["market"]["findings"]) or ["- Market data unavailable."],
        "Earnings & Fundamentals": _bullets(sp["earnings"]["findings"]) or ["- Fundamentals unavailable."],
        "News": [ctx["digest"]["summary"], *_bullets(sp["news"]["findings"])],
        "Changes since last run": changes,
        "Risks & Open Questions": _bullets(risks) or ["- No material risks flagged by the specialists (absence of evidence is not proof of safety)."],
        "Data gaps": _bullets(ctx["gaps"]) or ["- None detected."],
        "Caveats": ["- Automated summary of public data; not investment advice. Figures are only as fresh as the fetch times in the audit log."],
    }


def compose(ctx, skip=()):
    secs = build_sections(ctx)
    lines = [f"# {ctx['ticker']} Analyst Note ({ctx['run_date']})", ""]
    for name in ORDER:
        if name not in skip:
            lines += [f"## {name}", *secs[name], ""]
    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n"


def generate_draft(ctx, llm=None):
    if llm:
        out = (llm(WRITER_SYSTEM, json.dumps(compact(ctx), default=str)) or "").strip()
        if len(out) > 200:
            return out + "\n"
    learned = {"weak:balance", "weak:transparency", "weak:completeness"} & set(ctx["lesson_tags"])
    return compose(ctx, skip=() if learned else LEAN_SKIP)  # LEARNING: past lessons change the first draft


HEAD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s*(.+?)\s*#*\s*$")  # markdown heading, any level 1-6
BOLD_HEAD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:\*\*|__)(.+?)(?:\*\*|__)\s*:?\s*$")  # a line that is only **Bold**


def _norm_heading(text):
    """'## **1. Risks & Open Questions:**' -> 'risks & open questions' (bold, numbering, colon, case, spaces)."""
    t = re.sub(r"[*_`]", "", text).strip()
    t = re.sub(r"^\d+[.)]\s*", "", t)  # leading "1." or "2)"
    t = t.rstrip(":").strip().lower()
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t)


def sections(brief):
    """Split a note into {normalised heading: lines}.

    FIX: the original matched only lines beginning with exactly "## ", so LLM drafts using other
    heading styles returned no sections at all and every section was reported missing.
    """
    parts, cur = {}, None
    for line in brief.splitlines():
        m = HEAD_RE.match(line)
        name = _norm_heading(m.group(1)) if m else None
        if name is None:  # a bold-only line counts as a heading only if it names a known section
            b = BOLD_HEAD_RE.match(line)
            if b and any(_norm_heading(b.group(1)).startswith(k) for k in NAME_MAP):
                name = _norm_heading(b.group(1))
        if name:
            cur = name
            parts[cur] = []
        elif cur is not None:
            parts[cur].append(line)
    return parts


def _has(parts, prefix):
    return any(k.startswith(prefix) for k in parts)


def _get(parts, prefix):
    return next((v for k, v in parts.items() if k.startswith(prefix)), [])


def rule_evaluate(brief, ctx):
    parts, fb, sc = sections(brief), [], {}
    valid, bad, numeric, cited = set(ctx["valid_ids"]), set(), 0, 0
    for name, lines in parts.items():
        if name.startswith(("data gaps", "caveats")):
            continue
        for ln in lines:
            ids = cite_ids(ln)  # FIX: counts combined citations like [S2, S3]
            bad |= {i for i in ids if i not in valid}
            if re.search(r"\d", ln):
                numeric += 1
                cited += bool(ids)
    ratio = cited / numeric if numeric else 1.0
    sc["grounding"] = round(1 + 4 * ratio)
    if ratio < 1:
        fb.append(f"{numeric - cited} line(s) containing numbers have no [S#]/[N#] citation.")
    if bad:
        sc["grounding"] = min(sc["grounding"], 2)
        fb.append(f"Remove citations to unknown sources: {sorted(bad)}.")

    missing = [k for k in NAME_MAP if not _has(parts, k)]
    sc["completeness"] = round(1 + 4 * (len(NAME_MAP) - len(missing)) / len(NAME_MAP))
    if missing:
        fb.append("Missing sections: " + ", ".join(NAME_MAP[k] for k in missing) + ".")
    if brief.count("[") > brief.count("]"):  # ADDED: an unclosed citation bracket means the reply was cut off
        sc["completeness"] = min(sc["completeness"], 2)
        fb.append("Note looks truncated (unclosed '['): finish the last section and close every citation.")

    risk_bullets = [l for l in _get(parts, "risks") if l.strip().startswith(("-", "*", "•"))]  # FIX: "*" and "•" bullets too
    sc["balance"] = 5 if risk_bullets else 2
    if not risk_bullets:
        fb.append("Add a 'Risks & Open Questions' section with at least one bullet.")

    gtext = " ".join(_get(parts, "data gaps")).lower()
    if ctx["gaps"]:
        undisclosed = [g for g in ctx["gaps"] if g.split(":")[0].lower() not in gtext]
        sc["transparency"] = 5 if _has(parts, "data gaps") and not undisclosed else 2
        if sc["transparency"] < 5:
            fb.append("Disclose every data gap: " + "; ".join(ctx["gaps"]))
    else:
        sc["transparency"] = 5 if _has(parts, "data gaps") else 4

    ctext = " ".join(_get(parts, "changes since last run")).lower()
    sc["memory_use"] = 2 if ctx["prior"] and ("no prior run" in ctext or not ctext.strip()) else 5
    if sc["memory_use"] < 5:
        fb.append("A prior run exists: report what changed since it (metrics from memory).")
    return {"scores": sc, "feedback": fb}


def evaluate(brief, ctx, llm=None, threshold=4.0):
    ev = rule_evaluate(brief, ctx)
    if llm:
        j = parse_json(llm(JUDGE_SYSTEM, json.dumps({"note": brief, "evidence": compact(ctx)}, default=str)))
        if isinstance(j, dict) and isinstance(j.get("scores"), dict):
            for k in CRITERIA:
                v = j["scores"].get(k)
                if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and 1 <= v <= 5:
                    ev["scores"][k] = min(ev["scores"][k], round(v))
            ev["feedback"] += [x for x in j.get("feedback", []) if isinstance(x, str)][:5]
    ev["overall"] = round(sum(ev["scores"].values()) / len(CRITERIA), 2)
    ev["passed"] = ev["overall"] >= threshold and min(ev["scores"].values()) >= 3
    return ev


def _insert_missing(brief, ctx):
    parts, secs = sections(brief), build_sections(ctx)
    add = [t for k, t in NAME_MAP.items() if not _has(parts, k)]
    if not add:
        return brief
    block = "".join(f"## {t}\n" + "\n".join(secs[t]) + "\n\n" for t in add if t != "Caveats")
    out = brief.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    if "## Caveats" in out:
        return out.replace("## Caveats", block + "## Caveats", 1)
    tail = "## Caveats\n" + "\n".join(secs["Caveats"]) + "\n" if "Caveats" in add else ""
    return out + "\n" + block + tail


def refine(brief, feedback, ctx, llm=None):
    if llm:
        out = (llm(REFINE_SYSTEM, json.dumps({"note": brief, "feedback": feedback, "evidence": compact(ctx)},
                                              default=str)) or "").strip()
        if len(out) > 200:
            return out + "\n"
    return _insert_missing(brief, ctx)


def optimize(ctx, llm=None, max_iter=3, threshold=4.0):
    brief, history = generate_draft(ctx, llm), []
    for i in range(max_iter + 1):
        ev = evaluate(brief, ctx, llm, threshold)
        history.append({"iteration": i, **ev, "chars": len(brief)})
        if ev["passed"] or i == max_iter:
            break
        new = refine(brief, ev["feedback"], ctx, llm)
        if new.strip() == brief.strip():
            break
        brief = new
    return {"brief": brief, "history": history, "passed": history[-1]["passed"]}
