%%writefile research_agent.py
"""Autonomous Investment Research Agent.
PLAN -> ACT (dynamic tools, retry, re-plan) -> CHAIN (news) -> ROUTE (specialists) -> EVALUATE/OPTIMIZE -> REFLECT & LEARN.

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (research_agent.py):
- default_tools()["fetch_news"] now calls news_tools.fetch_news, which tries NewsAPI and falls back to Yahoo.
  Original called only fetch_news_newsapi, so a missing NEWSAPI_KEY was a hard failure.
- No other control-flow change. Plan, mandatory-tool safeguard, thin-news re-plan, reflect, and memory writes
  are as written. The ticker is whatever the caller passes; nothing here is ticker-specific.

Why: this orchestrator ties the four agent functions together: plan (including recall_memory),
dynamic tool use, self-reflection, and a memory write so the next run can improve.
"""

import json
import os
import uuid
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

import extra_tools as ex
import market_tools as mt
import news_tools as nt
from chain import run_news_chain
from evaluator import optimize
from llm import parse_json
from memory import MemoryStore
from router import TOOL_ROUTES, Router, run_specialists
from schema import ToolResult

MANDATORY = ["get_price_history", "get_fundamentals", "fetch_news"]
PLAN_SYSTEM = (
    "You are the planning module of an investment research agent. Choose which tools to call, in order, for the "
    "ticker. Use the lessons from past runs. Return JSON only: "
    '{"steps":[{"tool":"<name from catalog>","args":{},"why":"<short reason>"}]}')
REFLECT_SYSTEM = (
    "You are the agent reviewing your own run. Given the evaluation history and data gaps, return JSON only: "
    '{"assessment":"2 sentences on quality","lessons":["up to 3 short imperative lessons for the next run"]}')


def default_tools(news_file=None):
    def news(t, query=None):
        if news_file:
            return nt.load_headline_dump(news_file)
        # CHANGE: original was nt.fetch_news_newsapi only. fetch_news falls back to Yahoo.
        return nt.fetch_news(t, query=query)

    return {
        "get_price_history": {"fn": lambda t, period="6mo": mt.get_price_history(t, period=period),
                              "desc": "Daily OHLCV + trend/volatility metrics. args: period (e.g. 3mo, 6mo, 1y)",
                              "args": ["period"]},
        "get_fundamentals": {"fn": lambda t: mt.get_fundamentals(t),
                             "desc": "Market cap, P/E, EPS, next earnings date", "args": []},
        "fetch_news": {"fn": news, "desc": "Recent news articles. args: query (defaults to ticker)", "args": ["query"]},
        "get_macro": {"fn": lambda t: ex.get_macro(), "desc": "FRED macro indicators (needs FRED_API_KEY)", "args": []},
        "get_edgar_filings": {"fn": lambda t: ex.get_edgar_filings(t),
                              "desc": "Recent SEC filings (10-K/10-Q/8-K)", "args": []},
    }


class ResearchAgent:
    def __init__(self, ticker, llm=None, memory=None, tools=None, news_file=None,
                 log_dir="runs", max_refinements=3, threshold=4.0):
        self.ticker, self.llm = ticker.upper().strip(), llm
        self.memory = memory or MemoryStore()
        self.news_file, self.log_dir = news_file, log_dir
        self.max_refinements, self.threshold = max_refinements, threshold
        self.tools = dict(tools or default_tools(news_file))
        self.tools["recall_memory"] = {"fn": self._recall, "args": [],
                                       "desc": "RETRIEVAL: last run's metrics and lessons learned from memory"}
        self.trace = []

    def _recall(self, ticker):
        prior, lessons = self.memory.last_run(ticker), self.memory.get_lessons(ticker)
        return ToolResult.success("recall_memory", {
            "prior_run_id": prior["run_id"] if prior else None,
            "metrics": prior["metrics"] if prior else {}, "lessons": [l["text"] for l in lessons]}, "local memory")

    def _call(self, step):
        name, spec = step["tool"], self.tools.get(step["tool"])
        if not spec:
            return ToolResult.failure(name, "unknown tool")
        args = {k: v for k, v in step.get("args", {}).items() if k in spec.get("args", [])}

        def once():
            try:
                return spec["fn"](self.ticker, **args)
            except Exception as exc:
                return ToolResult.failure(name, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

        res, retried = once(), False
        if not res.ok and not any(x in (res.error or "") for x in ("not set", "401", "403", "unknown")):
            res, retried = once(), True
        self.trace.append({"phase": "tool", "tool": name, "args": args, "ok": res.ok, "error": res.error,
                           "retried": retried, "why": step.get("why", "")})
        return res

    def plan(self):
        prior, lessons = self.memory.last_run(self.ticker), self.memory.get_lessons(self.ticker)
        steps, mode = None, "rules"
        if self.llm:
            payload = {"ticker": self.ticker, "tools": {k: v["desc"] for k, v in self.tools.items()},
                       "lessons": [l["text"] for l in lessons], "has_prior_run": bool(prior)}
            parsed = parse_json(self.llm(PLAN_SYSTEM, json.dumps(payload)))
            parsed = parsed.get("steps") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
            if isinstance(parsed, list):
                steps = [{"tool": s["tool"], "args": s["args"] if isinstance(s.get("args"), dict) else {},
                          "why": s.get("why", "")} for s in parsed if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("tool") in self.tools]
                mode = "llm" if steps else "rules"
        if not steps:
            steps = self._rule_plan(prior, lessons)
        names = [s["tool"] for s in steps]
        for m in MANDATORY:
            if m not in names:
                steps.append({"tool": m, "args": {}, "why": "mandatory tool added by safeguard"})
        if "recall_memory" not in names:
            steps.insert(0, {"tool": "recall_memory", "args": {}, "why": "load prior metrics and lessons"})
        return steps, mode

    def _rule_plan(self, prior, lessons):
        tags = {l["tag"] for l in lessons}
        news_args = {}
        company = (prior or {}).get("metrics", {}).get("company")
        if "news_thin" in tags and company:
            news_args = {"query": f"{company} stock"}
        steps = [{"tool": "recall_memory", "args": {}, "why": "load prior metrics and lessons"},
                 {"tool": "get_price_history", "args": {}, "why": "price trend, volatility, moving averages"},
                 {"tool": "get_fundamentals", "args": {}, "why": "valuation and earnings date"},
                 {"tool": "fetch_news", "args": news_args, "why": "recent headlines" + (" (widened query, learned)" if news_args else "")}]
        if os.getenv("FRED_API_KEY") and "get_macro" in self.tools:
            steps.append({"tool": "get_macro", "args": {}, "why": "macro backdrop (FRED key present)"})
        if os.getenv("SEC_USER_AGENT") and "get_edgar_filings" in self.tools:
            steps.append({"tool": "get_edgar_filings", "args": {}, "why": "recent SEC filings"})
        return steps

    @staticmethod
    def _company(results, prior):
        for r in results:
            if r.tool == "get_fundamentals" and r.ok and r.data["fields"].get("name"):
                return r.data["fields"]["name"]
        return (prior or {}).get("metrics", {}).get("company")

    def _followups(self, results, executed, prior):
        company, news = self._company(results, prior), [r for r in results if r.tool == "fetch_news"]
        n = sum(len(r.data.get("articles", [])) for r in news if r.ok)
        query = f"{company} stock" if company else None
        already = any(s["tool"] == "fetch_news" and s.get("args", {}).get("query") == query for s in executed)
        if query and any(r.ok for r in news) and n < 5 and not self.news_file and not already:
            return [{"tool": "fetch_news", "args": {"query": query},
                     "why": f"only {n} article(s) found; widening query with company name"}]
        return []

    def reflect(self, ctx, opt, results):
        hist, rule_lessons = opt["history"], []
        for r in results:
            if not r.ok and r.tool != "recall_memory":
                rule_lessons.append({"tag": f"tool_failed:{r.tool}",
                                     "text": f"{r.tool} failed ({r.error}); check credentials/inputs or use a fallback."})
        n = len(ctx["digest"]["articles"])
        if n < 5:
            rule_lessons.append({"tag": "news_thin", "text": f"Only {n} usable news articles; widen the query with the company name or load a headline dump."})
        for k, v in hist[0]["scores"].items():
            if v < 4:
                rule_lessons.append({"tag": f"weak:{k}", "text": f"First draft scored {v}/5 on {k}; cover it in the first draft."})
        if len(hist) > 1:
            rule_lessons.append({"tag": "needed_refinement", "text": f"Draft needed {len(hist) - 1} refinement round(s) to pass."})
        final = hist[-1]
        weakest = min(final["scores"], key=final["scores"].get)
        assessment = (f"Final score {final['overall']}/5 ({'passed' if final['passed'] else 'NOT passed'}) after "
                      f"{len(hist) - 1} refinement(s); weakest criterion: {weakest}; {len(ctx['gaps'])} data gap(s).")
        llm_lessons = []
        if self.llm:
            j = parse_json(self.llm(REFLECT_SYSTEM, json.dumps({"history": [{k: h[k] for k in ("iteration", "scores", "feedback")} for h in hist],
                                                                 "gaps": ctx["gaps"]}, default=str)))
            if isinstance(j, dict):
                assessment = j.get("assessment") if isinstance(j.get("assessment"), str) else assessment
                llm_lessons = [x for x in j.get("lessons", []) if isinstance(x, str)][:3]
        return {"assessment": assessment, "rule_lessons": rule_lessons, "llm_lessons": llm_lessons}

    def run(self):
        run_id = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S-") + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
        prior = self.memory.last_run(self.ticker)
        lessons = self.memory.get_lessons(self.ticker)

        steps, mode = self.plan()
        self.trace.append({"phase": "plan", "mode": mode, "steps": steps})
        executed, results = list(steps), [self._call(s) for s in steps]
        for s in self._followups(results, executed, prior):
            self.trace.append({"phase": "replan", "step": s})
            executed.append(s)
            results.append(self._call(s))

        sources = {}
        for i, r in enumerate(results, 1):
            sources[f"S{i}"] = {"tool": r.tool, "source": r.source, "ok": r.ok, "error": r.error,
                                "warnings": r.warnings, "fetched_at": r.fetched_at}
        company = self._company(results, prior)

        digest = run_news_chain([r for r in results if r.tool == "fetch_news"], self.ticker, company, self.llm)

        items = [{"kind": "tool", "tool": r.tool, "sid": sid, "result": r}
                 for (sid, r) in zip(sources, results) if r.ok and r.tool in TOOL_ROUTES]
        items += [{"kind": "article", "sid": a["id"], "article": a} for a in digest["articles"]]
        buckets, route_log = Router().route(items)

        gaps = [f"{v['tool']}: {v['error']}" for v in sources.values() if not v["ok"]]
        gaps += [f"{v['tool']}: {w}" for v in sources.values() for w in v["warnings"]]
        if not digest["articles"] and not digest["errors"]:
            gaps.append("news: no relevant articles found")

        price = next((r for r in results if r.tool == "get_price_history"), None)
        fund = next((r for r in results if r.tool == "get_fundamentals"), None)
        metrics = mt.to_memory_metrics(price, fund)
        metrics.update({"company": company, "news_articles": len(digest["articles"])})
        memory_sid = next((k for k, v in sources.items() if v["tool"] == "recall_memory" and v["ok"]), None)

        ctx = {"ticker": self.ticker, "company": company, "run_date": date.today().isoformat(),
               "sources": sources, "digest": digest, "gaps": gaps,
               "valid_ids": list(sources) + [a["id"] for a in digest["articles"]],
               "memory_sid": memory_sid, "lessons": [l["text"] for l in lessons],
               "lesson_tags": [l["tag"] for l in lessons],
               "prior": {"run_id": prior["run_id"]} if prior else None,
               "changes": MemoryStore.diff(prior, metrics)}
        ctx["specialists"] = run_specialists(buckets, ctx)

        opt = optimize(ctx, self.llm, self.max_refinements, self.threshold)
        refl = self.reflect(ctx, opt, results)
        final = opt["history"][-1]
        self.memory.save_run(self.ticker, run_id, metrics, [a["title"] for a in digest["articles"]],
                             final["feedback"], opt["brief"], final["scores"])
        learned = self.memory.update_lessons(self.ticker, refl["rule_lessons"], refl["llm_lessons"])

        os.makedirs(self.log_dir, exist_ok=True)
        path = os.path.join(self.log_dir, f"{self.ticker}_{run_id}.json")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump({"run_id": run_id, "ticker": self.ticker, "trace": self.trace, "sources": sources,
                       "route_log": route_log, "news_chain": digest["stage_log"], "evaluation": opt["history"],
                       "reflection": refl, "lessons_saved": learned, "brief": opt["brief"]}, f, indent=2, default=str)
        return {"run_id": run_id, "brief": opt["brief"], "plan_mode": mode, "plan": steps, "route_log": route_log,
                "news_chain": digest["stage_log"], "evaluation": opt["history"], "reflection": refl,
                "lessons": learned, "audit_path": path}

%%writefile news_index.py
"""Optional FAISS index over the articles fetch_news already returned.

CHANGE LOG vs News_Ingestion_Pipeline.ipynb:
- This is a new module. The news notebook built the index inside a notebook cell and, on an empty
  Yahoo response, indexed a synthetic Apple earnings paragraph. That fallback is not here.
- Chunks are a retrieval side store. The agent still consumes article dicts from ToolResult.
- Zero-shot DeBERTa is not loaded. Category comes from news_tools.tag_category (keyword), which is
  the same signal the notebook's unused is_earnings_keyword was meant to provide. DeBERTa can be
  added later; it is not required for the chain or the router.
- save_local / load_local are real function calls, not markdown.
- FAISS is a retrieval side store only. The agent still consumes the article list from ToolResult;
  the index never invents documents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

SOURCE = "FAISS (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)"


def _documents(articles: list[dict]):
    from langchain_core.documents import Document
    from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

    splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=300, chunk_overlap=50)
    docs = []
    for i, a in enumerate(articles, 1):
        text = f"Title: {a.get('title', '')}\nSummary: {a.get('body', '')}"
        for chunk in splitter.split_text(text) or [text]:
            docs.append(Document(page_content=chunk, metadata={
                "article_id": f"A{i}", "title": a.get("title", ""), "url": a.get("url", ""),
                "publisher": a.get("source", ""), "published_at": a.get("published_at", ""),
                "category": a.get("category", "other"),
            }))
    return docs


def build_index(articles: list[dict], save_path: str | None = None):
    """Return (vector_db, n_chunks) or (None, 0) if there is nothing to index or the libs are missing.

    PEP 8 fix: the unused `as exc` binding is removed (flake8 F841). No behavior change.
    """
    if not articles:
        return None, 0  # CHANGE: news notebook injected fake docs here
    try:
        from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
        from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
    except ImportError:
        return None, 0  # libraries missing: fail closed, index nothing
    docs = _documents(articles)
    if not docs:
        return None, 0
    embed = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
    db = FAISS.from_documents(docs, embed)
    if save_path:
        os.makedirs(save_path, exist_ok=True)
        db.save_local(save_path)
    return db, len(docs)


def retrieve(db, query: str, k: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    """Cosine-similar chunks. Each hit keeps the parent article id so a note can still cite [N#] after join."""
    if db is None:
        return []
    hits = db.similarity_search_with_score(query, k=k)
    out = []
    for doc, score in hits:
        # FAISS L2 distance from LangChain; lower is closer. Report it as distance, not a fake probability.
        out.append({
            "article_id": doc.metadata.get("article_id"),
            "title": doc.metadata.get("title"),
            "url": doc.metadata.get("url"),
            "category": doc.metadata.get("category"),
            "published_at": doc.metadata.get("published_at"),
            "chunk": doc.page_content,
            "distance": round(float(score), 4),
        })
    return out

"""Offline tests. No network, no API keys. Run: python test_pipeline.py

CHANGE LOG vs Deepika Shrestha original (test_pipeline.py):
- Kept her chain, router, extra-tool, and agent-learning tests.
- ADDED test_router_between_phrase: the original "between of" headline must not reappear.
- ADDED test_empty_yahoo_shape: an empty-news failure carries no synthetic article text.
- ADDED test_tag_category: keyword tag lands in chain.py's category set.
- UPDATED test_rules_only_chain (2026-10-17): expects 3 articles, not 5, because the stricter
  preprocess relevance gate keeps only articles that name the company AND a financial keyword.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import chain
import extra_tools as ex
import market_tools as mt
import news_tools as nt
from memory import MemoryStore
from research_agent import ResearchAgent
from router import MarketSpecialist, Router
from schema import ToolResult


def make_df(n=120):
    idx = pd.bdate_range("2026-01-01", periods=n)
    c = 100 + np.arange(n) * 0.5
    return pd.DataFrame({"Open": c, "High": c + 1, "Low": c - 1, "Close": c, "Volume": np.full(n, 1e6)}, index=idx)


class FakeTicker:
    info = {"marketCap": 3e12, "trailingPE": 34.0, "forwardPE": 30.0, "trailingEps": 6.1,
            "shortName": "Acme Corp", "sector": "Tech", "currency": "USD"}
    calendar = {}

    def __init__(self, n=120):
        self.n = n

    def history(self, **kw):
        return make_df(self.n)


ARTICLES = [
    {"title": "Acme beats quarterly earnings estimates, raises guidance", "body": "Revenue rose 8% to $90 billion.", "source": "Wire", "published_at": "2026-09-28"},
    {"title": "Acme faces antitrust lawsuit from regulators", "body": "The DOJ probe concerns app store rules.", "source": "Wire2", "published_at": "2026-09-27"},
    {"title": "Analyst upgrades Acme, lifts price target", "body": "Acme rating raised to outperform.", "source": "Bank", "published_at": "2026-09-26"},
    {"title": "Acme unveils new product line", "body": "Acme launch event announces features.", "source": "Blog", "published_at": "2026-09-25"},
    {"title": "Acme unveils new product line", "body": "duplicate headline", "source": "Blog", "published_at": "2026-09-25"},
    {"title": "Fed signals rate cut as inflation cools", "body": "Acme shares gain on macro optimism.", "source": "News", "published_at": "2026-09-24"},
    {"title": "Unrelated company news", "body": "Nothing to see", "source": "X", "published_at": "2026-09-24"},
]


def tools(n=120, articles=ARTICLES):
    return {
        "get_price_history": {"fn": lambda t, period="6mo": mt.get_price_history(t, ticker_factory=lambda s: FakeTicker(n)),
                              "desc": "prices", "args": ["period"]},
        "get_fundamentals": {"fn": lambda t: mt.get_fundamentals(t, ticker_factory=lambda s: FakeTicker()),
                             "desc": "fundamentals", "args": []},
        "fetch_news": {"fn": lambda t, query=None: ToolResult.success(
            "fetch_news", {"query": query or t, "count": len(articles), "articles": articles}, "stub"),
            "desc": "news", "args": ["query"]},
    }


class ChainTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rules_only_chain(self):
        # CHANGE (2026-10-17): expected count 5 -> 3. The stricter preprocess gate keeps only
        # articles that name the company AND contain a financial keyword (earnings, antitrust,
        # analyst). The product, macro, and unrelated fixtures are dropped; the duplicate is deduped.
        r = ToolResult.success("fetch_news", {"articles": ARTICLES}, "stub")
        d = chain.run_news_chain([r], "ACME", "Acme Corp")
        ids = {a["id"] for a in d["articles"]}
        self.assertEqual(len(ids), 3)
        cats = {a["title"]: a["category"] for a in d["articles"]}
        self.assertEqual(cats["Acme beats quarterly earnings estimates, raises guidance"], "earnings")
        self.assertEqual(cats["Acme faces antitrust lawsuit from regulators"], "legal_regulatory")

    def test_no_news(self):
        d = chain.run_news_chain([ToolResult.failure("fetch_news", "401")], "ACME")
        self.assertEqual(d["articles"], [])
        self.assertIn("No usable", d["summary"])


class RouterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_routes(self):
        arts = [{"id": "N1", "category": "earnings"}, {"id": "N2", "category": "legal_regulatory"},
                {"id": "N3", "category": "analyst_rating"}]
        items = [{"kind": "article", "sid": a["id"], "article": a} for a in arts]
        items.append({"kind": "tool", "tool": "get_price_history", "sid": "S2", "result": None})
        items.append({"kind": "tool", "tool": "get_fundamentals", "sid": "S3", "result": None})
        b, log = Router().route(items)
        self.assertEqual([i["sid"] for i in b["earnings"]], ["N1", "N3", "S3"])
        self.assertEqual([i["sid"] for i in b["news"]], ["N2"])
        self.assertEqual([i["sid"] for i in b["market"]], ["S2"])

    def test_router_between_phrase(self):
        # CHANGE TEST: original headline template produced "between of".
        price = mt.get_price_history("ACME", ticker_factory=lambda s: FakeTicker(120))
        item = {"kind": "tool", "tool": "get_price_history", "sid": "S2", "result": price}
        out = MarketSpecialist().analyze([item], {"ticker": "ACME"})
        self.assertNotIn("between of", out["headline"])
        self.assertTrue("between the two averages" in out["headline"] or "above both" in out["headline"] or "below both" in out["headline"])


class NewsFixTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tag_category(self):
        self.assertEqual(nt.tag_category("Acme beats earnings", "revenue rose"), "earnings")
        self.assertEqual(nt.tag_category("Unrelated", "nothing here"), "other")
        self.assertIn(nt.tag_category("Analyst upgrades Acme", ""), set(chain.CATEGORIES))

    def test_empty_yahoo_shape(self):
        # The failure object is what the agent discloses. No synthetic body is attached.
        r = ToolResult.failure("fetch_news", "Yahoo returned 0 articles", "Yahoo Finance news (yfinance)")
        self.assertFalse(r.ok)
        self.assertNotIn("85.8", r.error)
        self.assertEqual(r.data, {})


class ExtraToolTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fred(self):
        fake = lambda url: {"observations": [{"date": "2026-08-01", "value": "."}, {"date": "2026-07-01", "value": "4.33"}]}
        r = ex.get_macro(("FEDFUNDS",), http_get=fake)
        self.assertTrue(r.ok)
        self.assertEqual(r.data["series"][0]["value"], 4.33)

    def test_edgar(self):
        def fake(url):
            if "company_tickers" in url:
                return {"0": {"cik_str": 320193, "ticker": "ACME", "title": "Acme"}}
            return {"filings": {"recent": {"form": ["8-K", "4", "10-Q"], "filingDate": ["2026-09-01", "2026-08-30", "2026-08-01"],
                                           "accessionNumber": ["1-1-1", "2-2-2", "3-3-3"], "primaryDocument": ["a.htm", "b.htm", "c.htm"]}}}
        r = ex.get_edgar_filings("acme", http_get=fake)
        self.assertEqual([f["form"] for f in r.data["filings"]], ["8-K", "10-Q"])


class AgentTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_learning_across_runs_offline(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            mem = MemoryStore(os.path.join(d, "m.json"))
            first = ResearchAgent("ACME", memory=mem, tools=tools(120), log_dir=d).run()
            h1 = first["evaluation"]
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(h1), 2)
            self.assertTrue(h1[-1]["passed"])
            second = ResearchAgent("ACME", memory=mem, tools=tools(130), log_dir=d).run()
            self.assertEqual(len(second["evaluation"]), 1)
            self.assertNotIn("between of", second["brief"])
            self.assertNotIn("No prior run", second["brief"].split("## Changes since last run")[1].split("##")[0])

    def test_tool_failure_is_disclosed(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            t = tools()
            t["fetch_news"]["fn"] = lambda tk, query=None: ToolResult.failure("fetch_news", "Yahoo returned 0 articles", "Yahoo")
            out = ResearchAgent("ACME", memory=MemoryStore(os.path.join(d, "m.json")), tools=t, log_dir=d).run()
            self.assertIn("Yahoo returned 0 articles", out["brief"].split("## Data gaps")[1])
            self.assertNotIn("85.8", out["brief"])

4 — Offline tests (no keys, no network)¶

These are Deepika's tests plus three regression checks: the router phrase, the empty-news failure shape (no synthetic article), and the keyword category tag. The chain test now expects 3 articles because the stricter relevance gate drops the product, macro, and unrelated fixtures. Together they confirm the router fix, the fail-closed news path, and learning across runs without live keys or network. Expected output: Ran 10 tests and OK.

5 — Run the agent¶

Two runs on TICKER. The cell below first clears ./ira_state/ (FRESH_START = True), so Run 1 is a true first run with no memory from earlier sessions. That makes the learning step visible: Run 1 writes lessons, and Run 2 reads them. Run 2 must show a "Changes since last run" section that is not "No prior run", which is the memory requirement. Memory and audit logs go under ./ira_state/. If you mount Drive and point STATE there, set FRESH_START = False after the graded run so memory is kept.

The first run exercises plan → tools → chain → route → evaluate → reflect, and writes the memory file that the second run will read. The LLM status line says whether Gemini answered or the rule fallbacks were used.

import importlib  # reload so edits to the written files are what this process imports
import shutil  # used once below to clear old memory for a clean graded run

import chain
import evaluator
import memory
import news_tools
import research_agent
import router

for m in (news_tools, chain, router, evaluator, memory, research_agent):
    importlib.reload(m)  # pick up %%writefile output

# These imports must follow the reload so they bind to the freshly written classes.
from llm import make_llm  # Gemini if GEMINI_API_KEY is set, else None
from memory import MemoryStore  # JSON store keyed by ticker
from research_agent import ResearchAgent  # Host orchestrator (Deepika)

STATE = "ira_state"  # change to a Drive path if you mounted Drive; default is the Colab disk
FRESH_START = True  # Why: Graded run starts with no old memory, so Run 1 is a real first run
if FRESH_START:
    shutil.rmtree(STATE, ignore_errors=True)  # deletes only this notebook's ira_state folder
    print("Fresh start: cleared", STATE)


def llm_status(model, run):
    """One-line disclosure of whether Gemini answered or the rule fallbacks ran."""
    if model is None:
        return "LLM status: rule-based mode (no GEMINI_API_KEY)."
    note = f"LLM status: {model.model}, {model.calls} call(s) so far; plan_mode = {run['plan_mode']}."
    if getattr(model, "truncated", 0):  # ADDED: replies cut off at max_output_tokens
        note += f" Truncated replies: {model.truncated}."
    if model.last_error:  # llm.py returns "" on errors, so the agent silently uses rules
        note += f" Most recent LLM error/warning: {model.last_error[:200]}"
    return note


llm = make_llm("gemini")  # None when the secret is absent; rule path still runs
print(type(llm).__name__ + " (" + llm.model + ")" if llm else "Rule-based mode (no GEMINI_API_KEY)")

agent = ResearchAgent(  # ticker comes only from the ticker cell
    TICKER, llm=llm,
    memory=MemoryStore(f"{STATE}/memory.json"),  # enduring across the two runs in this session
    log_dir=f"{STATE}/runs",
)
run1 = agent.run()  # plan -> tools -> chain -> route -> evaluate -> reflect
print(run1["brief"])  # the cited note
print("plan_mode:", run1["plan_mode"], "| evaluations:", len(run1["evaluation"]),
      "| passed:", run1["evaluation"][-1]["passed"], "| audit:", run1["audit_path"])
print(llm_status(llm, run1))

import json  # compact one-line printing of the chain stage log

for name, run in (("RUN 1", run1), ("RUN 2", run2)):
    print(f"===== {name}: PLAN (mode: {run['plan_mode']}) =====")  # agent function 1: planning
    for i, step in enumerate(run["plan"], 1):  # each tool the planner chose, with its reason
        print(f"  {i}. {step['tool']} {step.get('args') or ''} - {step.get('why', '')}")

    print("  PROMPT CHAIN stages:")  # workflow 1: ingest -> preprocess -> classify -> extract -> summarize
    for stage in run["news_chain"]:  # stage_log written by chain.run_news_chain
        print("   ", json.dumps(stage))

    print("  ROUTING log:")  # workflow 2: which specialist received each item, and why
    for r in run["route_log"]:  # one row per tool result or article
        print(f"    {r['item']:>4} -> {r['to']}  ({r['why']})")

    print("  EVALUATOR-OPTIMIZER history:")  # workflow 3 and self-reflection
    for h in run["evaluation"]:  # one row per draft: scores 1-5, pass flag, feedback used to refine
        print(f"    iter {h['iteration']}: overall={h['overall']} passed={h['passed']} scores={h['scores']}")
        for fb in h["feedback"]:
            print(f"      feedback: {fb}")

    print("  REFLECTION:", run["reflection"]["assessment"])  # agent function 3: self-reflection
    print("  LESSONS saved to memory:")  # agent function 4; LLM lessons all share the tag "llm", so show their text
    for lesson in run["lessons"]:
        print("    -", lesson["tag"] if lesson.get("source") != "llm" else "llm: " + lesson["text"][:100])
    print()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

import market_tools as mt  # Price tool the agent called

period = next((s.get("args", {}).get("period") for s in run1["plan"]  # ADDED: same window the agent used
               if s.get("tool") == "get_price_history" and s.get("args", {}).get("period")), "6mo")
price = mt.get_price_history(TICKER, period=period)  # One extra call; ToolResult never raises
saved_close = MemoryStore(f"{STATE}/memory.json").last_run(TICKER)["metrics"].get("last_close")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 4.5))  # Three panels side by side

if price.ok:  # panel 1: close with 20/50-day averages (Market specialist inputs, [S2])
    hist = pd.DataFrame(price.data["history"]).set_index("date")["close"]  # date -> close
    axes[0].plot(hist.index, hist.values, label="Close")
    axes[0].plot(hist.index, hist.rolling(20).mean(), label="20-day avg")
    axes[0].plot(hist.index, hist.rolling(50).mean(), label="50-day avg")
    axes[0].set_xticks(hist.index[::25])  # thin the date labels so they stay readable
    axes[0].tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
    axes[0].legend()
    print("Chart last close:", price.data["metrics"]["last_close"], "| close saved by run 2:", saved_close)
else:
    axes[0].text(0.5, 0.5, "Price fetch failed: " + str(price.error), ha="center", wrap=True)
axes[0].set_title(f"{TICKER} price and moving averages")

drafts = (("Run 1 first draft", run1["evaluation"][0]),  # panel 2: evaluator-optimizer scores
          ("Run 1 final", run1["evaluation"][-1]),
          ("Run 2 first draft", run2["evaluation"][0]),
          ("Run 2 final", run2["evaluation"][-1]))  # ADDED: shows the effect of Run 2's refinement
criteria = list(run1["evaluation"][0]["scores"])  # grounding, completeness, balance, transparency, memory_use
styles = (("o", "-"), ("s", "--"), ("^", "-."), ("D", ":"))  # distinct marker and line style per draft
for i, ((label, h), (mk, ls)) in enumerate(zip(drafts, styles)):
    offset = (i - 1.5) * 0.06  # small shift so identical scores don't hide each other
    x = [j + offset for j in range(len(criteria))]
    axes[1].plot(x, [h["scores"][c] for c in criteria], marker=mk, linestyle=ls, label=label)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(len(criteria)))
axes[1].set_xticklabels(criteria)
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 5.5)  # scores are 1-5; pass = average >= 4 and none below 3
axes[1].set_title("Evaluator-optimizer scores (1-5)")
axes[1].legend()

routed = collections.Counter(r["to"] for r in run1["route_log"] if str(r["item"]).startswith("N"))
if routed:  # panel 3: routing split
    axes[2].bar(list(routed), list(routed.values()))
else:  # fail closed: no articles means nothing was routed (see Data gaps)
    axes[2].text(0.5, 0.5, "No articles routed (see Data gaps)", ha="center")
axes[2].yaxis.set_major_locator(plt.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
axes[2].set_ylabel("Articles")
axes[2].set_title("Run 1 articles routed to each specialist")

plt.tight_layout()  # keep titles from overlapping in the PDF export
plt.show()

8 — Evaluation and Iteration: results, fixes, and lessons learned¶

Run summary (TICKER = AAPL, Colab, Sunday Oct 18, 2026, about 9:11 AM PT; Gemini gemini-3.8-flash). The agent wrote a cited analyst note twice from one memory file, starting from an empty ira_state/. Every figure cites a source id: [S#] for tool results and [N#] for news articles.

Agent functions shown above

  • Plan: Gemini planned both runs and gave a reason for each step. Run 1 had 6 steps: recall_memory → get_fundamentals → get_price_history (1y) → fetch_news → get_edgar_filings → get_macro. Run 2 also had 6 steps but reordered them (get_edgar_filings before fetch_news). Its reasons draw on memory, for example "Retrieve prior run baselines, key metrics, and historical lessons learned for comparison" and "regulatory updates, risks, and concrete operational headwinds". A safeguard adds any mandatory tool the planner leaves out. Thin news (fewer than 5 relevant articles) triggers a widened re-query. It did not fire here because 6 of the 12 articles were relevant.
  • Tools: In Run 1: memory recall [S1], Yahoo Finance fundamentals [S2] and prices [S3], NewsAPI headlines [S4] (12 articles), SEC EDGAR filings [S5], and FRED macro [S6]. Run 2 used the same tools; because of the new order, EDGAR is [S4] and news is [S5]. Every tool returns a ToolResult, and a failure becomes a Data gap, not an error.
  • Self-reflection: The evaluator scores each draft from 1 to 5 on grounding, completeness, balance, transparency, and memory use (pass = average ≥ 4.0 and no score below 3). The reflection step turns those scores into lessons. After Run 1 it noted that "data limitations and baseline memory conditions were clearly delineated without introducing ungrounded speculation."
  • Learning across runs: Run 1 saved three LLM lessons: map every figure to a citation, pair growth catalysts directly against concrete operational headwinds, and document data limits and missing prior-run baselines. Run 2 read them. Its plan and Summary both use the catalyst-vs-headwind framing ("these tailwinds are directly balanced by concrete operational headwinds"). Its "Changes since last run" section reads "No change in tracked metrics since run 20261018T161147-1109c4 [S1]" instead of "No prior run to compare." Run 2 added three lessons of its own. Memory keeps the five newest unique LLM lessons, so after Run 2 it holds Run 2's three and two of Run 1's.

Workflow patterns shown above

  • Prompt chaining: ingest 12 → preprocess (dedupe, then a company/ticker and financial-keyword gate) keeps 6 → classify → extract → summarize. Gemini handled all of it (6/6 articles at each stage, 0 rule fallbacks), in both runs. Each stage has a gate and a rule fallback.
  • Routing: Price and macro go to the Market specialist (S3, S6). Fundamentals, filings, and earnings/analyst articles go to Earnings & Fundamentals (S2, S5, N3 analyst rating, N5 earnings). The other categories go to News (N1 product, N2 legal/regulatory, N4 and N6 other). Run 2 routed the same way; it tagged N4 as product, and EDGAR was S4.
  • Evaluator–optimizer: In this final run, both first drafts passed at 5.0/5 on all five criteria (one evaluation per run), so the refine step was not needed and did not fire. Panel 2 therefore shows four overlapping lines. The loop did refine in our previous full run (Oct 17, 2026, about 6:40 PM PT). There, Run 2's first draft scored 4.4/5 and failed on memory use (2) because the writer had not been told a prior run existed. One refinement raised it to 5.0/5. After we fixed that cause (see the prior-run fix below), Run 2's first draft passed on its own. Both final notes have all eight sections and end with Caveats.

Integration issues fixed while combining the two teammate notebooks

  • The router headline said "trading between of its averages". Phrases are now complete (regression test added).
  • Invalid Claude model id claude-sonnet-5-5 → claude-sonnet-4-5 (Gemini is the path used here).
  • The agent called NewsAPI only. Now it tries NewsAPI first, with Yahoo as the fallback.
  • When Yahoo returned nothing, the news notebook indexed a synthetic "$85.8 billion" Apple article. That's removed; an empty fetch is now a reported data gap.
  • A DIS test run pulled non-financial articles. Fix: a generic financial NewsAPI query, a post-fetch relevance filter, and a two-signal preprocess gate (works for any ticker). The notes now draw only on relevant financial articles.
  • The Summary said "No news retrieved" while the News section listed articles, because routing sends earnings/analyst articles to the Earnings specialist. The News specialist now checks the full chain output.
  • In Gemini mode the evaluator scored complete notes 2.8/5 with "Missing sections: all 8" because it expected exact headings. The section check now accepts heading variants, and the writer prompt names the headings.
  • Combined citations such as [S2, S3] were not counted. The evaluator and the chain now parse them.
  • Long Gemini replies could be cut off. The output limit is now 8192 tokens (up from 4096), and truncated replies (MAX_TOKENS) are flagged and reported in the LLM status line.
  • Repeated lessons piled up in memory. They are now de-duplicated in order.
  • The Gemini writer was never told that a prior run existed, so Run 2 claimed memory held no prior metrics. It now receives the prior run id and the "Changes since last run" lines, and in this run Run 2 named Run 1's id.
  • Fallback to rules was originally silent. An LLM status line after each run now prints the model and call count, plus any truncated replies or the last error.
  • The offline test was updated for the stricter relevance gate. All 10 offline tests pass (section 4).

Lessons learned

  • Fail closed: a visible data gap is better than an invented article or citation.
  • One shared contract (ToolResult, [S#]/[N#]) is what made two separate notebooks integrable.
  • Test the fallback paths (no LLM reply, empty Yahoo feed, no news) - that's where the bugs were. Print which path ran (the LLM status line) so troubleshooting is possible.
  • A rule-based checker must tolerate how an LLM formats its output, or it will grade good work as missing.
  • Check every summary line against the section it summarizes, and tell the LLM everything memory knows. Fixing the writer's context did more than the refine loop: Run 2 went from needing a refinement to passing on its first draft.
  • Run from a fresh memory state before exporting, so the learning step is visible.

Limitations. Gemini answered all 14 calls with no errors or truncated replies, so both notes come from the LLM path; the offline tests exercise the rule path. The Gemini judge gave every draft 5/5, so the refine loop was not exercised in this run, and the judge may be lenient. Its scores measure citation coverage and completeness, not forecast accuracy. Both runs used the same market data (Friday Oct 16 close), so no tracked metric changed between runs. EDGAR ran with the default contact User-Agent because SEC_USER_AGENT was not set, and SEC asks for a real contact. Yahoo news is often empty from Colab IPs (NewsAPI supplied the articles here). The FAISS side index built 20 chunks from the 12 NewsAPI articles. The Hugging Face token warning in section 7 only means the MiniLM model was downloaded unauthenticated. Memory lives in the Colab session unless STATE points to Drive. This is not investment advice.
